description:
ABOUT NEXGEN CLOUD 

NexGen Cloud is a fast-growing GPU cloud and AI infrastructure business. We're the company behind Hyperstack — a self-serve, on-demand cloud platform built for high-performance AI, HPC, and compute-heavy workloads. Powered by 100% renewable energy and NVIDIA architecture, Hyperstack gives teams from AI startups to enterprise the compute they need, without the cost or complexity of legacy cloud.

We move fast, solve hard problems, and build things that matter. If you want ownership, real impact, and a front-row seat to one of the most consequential infrastructure shifts of the decade — this is the place.

THE ROLE: DATA CENTRE DEPLOYMENT LEAD 

We're building GPU clusters across multiple international regions, and none of that capacity reaches customers until it's racked, cabled, commissioned and handed over. Our Senior Deployment Lead owns the pipeline but can't be on every site at once, so we need a senior onsite authority who can lead each build and hold every region to the same standard.

This is a role for someone who's happiest on the data centre floor making the call, not waiting for one. You'll lead a team of 3–5 Deployment Engineers through each build, catch problems at planning before hardware lands, and hand over sites that Operations can run from day two. Expect around 50% international travel, remote-first in between.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING 

Rather than a checklist, here's what success in this role actually looks like:

- Own each site as the onsite decision-maker, leading Deployment Engineers day to day, directing contractors safely, and escalating only what genuinely sits beyond onsite authority.

- Collaborate closely with the Senior Deployment Lead, Network Engineering, Procurement & Supply Chain, and Data Centre Operations/NOC to take every build from validated design to clean handover.

- Validate design plans and BOMs before hardware arrives, checking space, power, cooling, weight and interoperability (optics, AOC, DAC) so issues are fixed at planning, not on site.

- Produce and validate structured and fibre cabling designs, including length estimates, oversee cable pathing, and run cabling QC so every install matches the design before sign-off.

- Oversee racking and installation of GPU servers and network hardware, support fabric installation and cutover, and make sure commissioning meets the agreed acceptance criteria.

- Define and enforce the deployment standards every region builds to — rack, cabling, labelling and documentation — and hand over every site with complete as-built records.

- Run post-deployment reviews, turn the findings into better workflows, and develop your engineers so the team takes on more of each build over time.

ABOUT YOU 

We care more about how you think and work than a perfect CV. You'll likely bring a combination of the following:

Essential: 

- Experience leading a technical deployment team on site — allocating work and acting as the onsite authority, not just the most experienced engineer on the crew.

- Advanced structured and fibre cabling experience, including producing designs, estimating lengths and running QC.

- Experience creating and reviewing BOMs against space, power, cooling, weight and interoperability, including optics, AOC and DAC.

- Significant data centre deployment experience, with strong network and server hardware knowledge, and a track record of writing or enforcing standards and documentation others followed.

- Willingness to travel internationally around 50% of the time (sometimes at short notice, for days or weeks at a time), and fluent English with clear written reporting.

Nice to Have: 

- GPU or HPC cluster build experience, ideally including InfiniBand and fat-tree or rail-optimised fabric designs.

description:

About the role

As an Applied Research Engineer in our Video team, you will help build the next generation of production-grade foundation models for human-centric video generation.

You will join a highly focused team working at the intersection of large-scale generative modeling, distributed systems, and production engineering. Our mission is to develop and optimize video base models that power realistic, controllable, and emotionally expressive synthetic humans at scale.

This is not pure research. This is applied research with direct product impact.

You will work on advancing training recipes, scaling distributed systems, improving evaluation frameworks, and optimizing inference to ensure our models are high quality, stable, and efficient enough for real-world deployment. Your work will directly influence models used by tens of thousands of businesses worldwide.

You will own and execute end-to-end research and engineering projects, from hypothesis to production impact. This includes:

- Developing and scaling latent video diffusion models tailored for human-centric video generation

- Designing conditioning mechanisms to improve control (pose, emotion, script, camera) without sacrificing fidelity

- Advancing distributed training strategies (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, sequence parallelism) under real compute constraints

- Improving training stability at multi-node scale

- Designing rigorous evaluation frameworks combining automated metrics and structured human evaluation

- Optimizing inference for low latency, high resolution, and cost efficiency 

- Running controlled ablations and experiments to drive high-signal modeling decisions

- Contributing to high engineering standards: reproducibility, experiment tracking, CI/CD, monitoring

You will be expected to move fast, run multiple hypotheses in parallel, identify signal early, and focus on outcomes rather than exploration for its own sake.

What we’re looking for 

Must-have

- Strong experience training deep learning models at scale

- Strong Python and PyTorch skills

- Hands-on experience with diffusion models (image domain required; video preferred)

- Experience with large scale multi-GPU / multi-node training

- Good understanding of distributed training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed or similar)

- Ability to design controlled experiments and interpret noisy results

Nice-to-have

- Experience with video diffusion models

- Experience in avatar or human-centric generation

- Familiarity with world / interactive models

- Experience with GANs or VAEs

Experience optimizing inference systems for production

Our stack

- Python, PyTorch, CUDA

- DeepSpeed, distributed training & inference

- Sequence parallelism

- AWS, SLURM, Docker

- GitHub, CI/CD pipelines

Who you are

- You are research-driven but outcome-focused

- You care about shipping, not just publishing

- You can explore multiple ideas quickly and drop low-signal directions early

- You communicate clearly and present results scientifically

- You operate independently but collaborate actively across teams

Why join us?

- Build production-scale video foundation models in a fast-growing Generative AI company

- Work on human-centric video generation with real-world impact

- Tackle hard problems in scaling, stability, and controllability

- Influence the direction of next-generation synthetic human technology

If you want to work on cutting-edge generative video models and see your research power real-world products, we’d love to talk.

Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. title: Scientific Product Director, Clinical Prediction
description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with the world's largest cohort of patient tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our AI-powered predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical trial outcomes, validate therapies, and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we deliver insights that consistently outperform existing solutions.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them - and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalized. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

The role

Our clinical-prediction offer gives pharma partners the evidence to guide decisions before and during clinical development. We are looking for a Scientific Product Director to turn this science into sellable products: decide what gets developed and when, define what each capability can claim and output, and shape how results are delivered to partners.

You will report to Gustave Ronteix, CTO and co-founder, and work daily with a tight-knit interdisciplinary team composed of Computational Biology, Data Science, R&D, Platform Strategy & Operations, BD and Pharma Partnerships.

What you'll do

1. Own the product roadmap 

- Design and build a scalable product capable of derisking and accelerating clinical development of drug candidates based on Orakl’s scientific capabilities

- Turn signals from BD, Pharma Partnerships and R&D into capability definitions: specs, target metrics, validation plan, in- vs out-of-scope definition, cost to deliver

- Set priorities and dates with Engineering and Data Science; flag slippage early and make the trade-offs

- Identify productization-gaps from delivery audits and analysis, and feed recurring ones back into the roadmap

2. Oversee product maturity and decide what we sell 

- Maintain the capability catalog: what is available now, in beta or on the roadmap, and what each can and cannot claim

- Contribute to the final decision of when a capability is ready to sell (based on Data Science’s validation evidence) versus what is not-yet sellable in the pipeline, and communicate it internally

- Oversee the scientific case for each capability: white papers, application notes, posters

3. Design how results reach partners 

- Design the reports, data packages and dashboards partners receive, and direct the engineers who build them

- Own the deliverable contents: figures, statistical summaries, methods, limitations

- Embed the approved claims and the QC checklist in every template, so Pharma Partnerships can produce a correct deliverable at scale

- Keep templates current as the validated envelope changes, and pull or revise one when it no longer applies

What we're looking for

Must have

- PhD or equivalent in cancer biology, pharmacology, biostatistics or computational biology

- 8+ years in translational oncology, biomarker or diagnostics development, computational-biology platforms or preclinical CRO services, including 2+ owning a product roadmap 

- Technical depth: you read and understand production code, and can brief and review the work of engineers who build our reports and dashboards

- You judge evidence: from a validation pack - back-tests, calibration, biomarker cutoffs -, you can state a claim the data supports and refuse the one it doesn't

- You have experience working at the intersection of scientific and business departments within fast-growing companies

- You know how pharma decides: you have seen proposals, SOWs and due-diligence questions, and know what a go/no-go decision needs from a prediction

- Fluent in English 

Nice to have

- You have seen bespoke research work turned into something repeatable and sellable

- Scientific authorship : Posters, talks, papers or white papers; a presence at AACR, ASCO, ESMO or SITC

- Regulatory: exposure to regulated or quality-managed environments

- Therapeutic or preclinical knowledge : ADC, immuno-oncology or targeted therapy; organoid or in-vitro pharmacology

- Clinical-trial design or Trial statistics: adaptive designs, sample size, endpoints

- Templated reporting : report-generation frameworks or web front-end

What we offer

- Mission: work on the forefront of cancer research.

- Ownership: a product function to build from the ground up.

- Impact: pharma teams make real portfolio decisions with what you define.

- Team: an exceptional crew of clinicians, biologists, engineers and data scientists, most with a PhD.

title: Equipment Engineer - Automation
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Missions and activities of the position 

1. Project phase – owner's engineer for Maintenance 

- Represent Maintenance in every phase of new equipment projects (starting with the MRS1 cross-belt sorter), from design reviews to FAT, SAT, commissioning and ramp-up. For the sorter, whose design is already set, take over the installed system and optimise it after go-live.

- Work side by side with the OEM / integrator engineers: collect technical knowledge, challenge design choices, maintainability, access, spare-part strategy and the proposed maintenance plan before they are frozen.

- Define and verify the Maintenance acceptance criteria (documentation, training, spare parts, safety, availability targets). The Maintenance sign-off is mandatory: no handover to operations without it.

- Track and drive to closure the technical punch list and warranty issues raised during commissioning and the warranty period.

2. Technical file & spare parts 

- Build and own the equipment technical file: as-built electrical and mechanical drawings, PLC and software versions, parameter backups, network architecture, safety documentation, OEM manuals.

- Create the asset hierarchy and criticality analysis in the CMMS.

- Define the critical spare-parts list (references, min/max stock, lead times) and keep it up to date.

- Reduce dependency on the OEM: identify and qualify second-source suppliers for critical parts, run compatibility tests and document equivalences.

- Propose spare-parts and supplier decisions to the Maintenance Manager; after an initial period, take these decisions autonomously within agreed limits, with the Maintenance Manager's validation.

3. Maintenance strategy & procedures 

- Write and maintain preventive maintenance plans, corrective procedures and troubleshooting guides for the equipment family, based on OEM data, FMEA and field experience.

- Monitor equipment performance (availability, MTBF, MTTR, top failure modes), lead root-cause analysis on recurring or major failures and implement permanent corrective actions.

- Challenge the original design when needed and drive engineering changes: retrofits, drive and firmware updates, software or parameter optimisation, with the OEM and internal stakeholders.

4. Training & technical support 

- Train the operational maintenance team (technicians and operatives) on the equipment, its software/HMI and the troubleshooting procedures; validate their autonomy level.

- Act as the level-2 / level-3 technical expert for the equipment family on site and remotely, across sites.

5. Escalation, vendor & SLA management 

- Own technical escalations through to resolution: with the Tetris team (Vinted's internal tools and sorting logic) when the issue is on the software or data side, and with OEM / integrator support (SAV) when it is on the equipment side.

- Lead the diagnosis that tells which side an issue comes from (equipment, controls, Vinted software), with facts and data.

- Work within the after-sales and maintenance agreements already in place with OEMs: make the most of them day to day, monitor performance against SLAs and warranty terms, feed lessons learned into future renewals, and provide the technical evidence to the program managers, who own the contractual relationship.

- Prepare and lead technical review meetings with OEMs and integrators.

6. Safety & compliance 

- Ensure the equipment and its maintenance comply with machine safety requirements (CE marking, safety functions, lock-out/tag-out) and site H&S standards.

- Support safety audits and regulatory inspections, and drive the resulting corrective actions to completion.

Occasional responsibilities 

- Take ownership of additional equipment families (e.g. conveyors, AMR fleets, Monk lines) once the cross-belt is stable.

- Support pre-project technical due diligence on new equipment (specifications, vendor benchmarks, maintainability review).

- Participate in the hiring and onboarding of maintenance technicians and future engineers.

Interests, constraints, difficulties of the position 

- High-visibility role on new strategic automation investments.

- Site-based in an operational warehouse, with regular presence on the shop floor.

- Regular travel to MRS1, OEM premises (FAT) and other Vinted Go sites, especially during commissioning.

- Day-based role, no on-call. Flexibility needed during commissioning, ramp-up and major incidents (possible early, late or weekend work).

- Needs to influence without authority: OEMs, integrators, IT and program management teams.

Your profile 

Knowledge & experience 

- Engineering degree (Master's / Bac+5) in automation, electrical, mechatronics or industrial engineering, or Bac+2/3 with equivalent proven experience.

- At least 3 years' experience, ideally 5 or more, as Equipment Engineer, Automation Engineer, Tool Owner or Maintenance/Reliability Engineer in a highly automated environment: parcel sortation and intralogistics, airport baggage handling, logistics or other automated industries.

- Automation background required.

- Proven involvement in at least one industrial equipment project from FAT/SAT to ramp-up, working with OEMs or integrators.

Technical skills 

- Able to read and diagnose complete PLC and HMI programs (Siemens TIA Portal and/or Rockwell, Beckhoff) and to make controlled modifications; industrial networks (Profinet, Profibus, EtherCAT, Ethernet/IP).

- Drives (parameters, firmware), servo motors, sensors, scanners / DWS, pneumatics; reading electrical and mechanical schematics.

- Retrofit experience and component qualification (equivalence, compatibility testing)

- Safety PLCs and machine safety functions.

- Understanding of the interfaces between equipment controls, SCADA/WCS and IT systems.

- Reliability methods: FMEA, RCA (5 Why, Ishikawa, 8D), criticality analysis; CMMS and PM planning.

- Sortation equipment experience (cross-belt, tilt-tray, shoe sorters) is a strong plus.

- French electrical certification (habilitation électrique BR / B2V / BC) or ability to obtain it.

- Fluent French and professional English (OEMs and the Vinted Go network work in English).

Behavioural skills 

- Strong ownership: treats the equipment as their own, from design to end of life.

- Able to challenge OEM and integrator engineers constructively, with facts and data.

- Structured and disciplined in documentation.

- Good teacher: enjoys transferring knowledge to technicians.

- Calm and solution-oriented under production pressure; strong safety mindset.

Please note: the main tasks and skills identified and noted in the function described above may need to evolve depending on the constraints and organisation specific to the company and its environment. They are, therefore, indicative and not contractual. 

Working at Vinted 

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Equal opportunity 

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

The annual gross salary range for this position is:

€45.000 — €60.000 EUR

title: Devops Engineer
description:
As a DevOps Engineer, you will be an integral part of an existing team comprising sixseven DevOps professionals. You will play a vital role in designing, implementing, and maintaining our cloud infrastructure and the internal platform built on it, which serves over 1800+ client companies, with 2.5+ million registered users and 30,000 daily active users. 

You will collaborate closely with all engineering squads including Development, Architecture, AI, and Data teams, to ensure the smooth and efficient delivery of our SaaS product. Our objective is to treat our infrastructure as a product for our developers, managing its complexity so they don’t have to. We provide simple, ready-to-use tools that enable them to build, deploy, and run their services efficiently.. Your expertise will be crucial in driving continuous improvement and fostering innovation within our DevOps and Platform Engineering practices.

You will have the opportunity to: 

- Make a tangible impact in a rapidly evolving company. You will be responsible for building and maintaining a scalable infrastructure (accommodating more developers, more customers, and expansion into more countries) while optimizing resources (monitoring costs, reducing toil, and improving time to market) to support our growing activities. 

- Engage in the continuous enhancement of our practices and undertake challenging and comprehensive projects. If you are interested in topics like SRE practices and platform engineering, you will play a key role in our transformation. 

- Establish your own niche within a highly-skilled team that is eager to learn, share knowledge, and progress together. 

Within 1 month, you will 

- Discover 360Learning, its platform, its teams and its culture.

- Become familiar with our R&D way of working.

- Understand the team’s processes.

Within 3 months, you will 

- Automate infrastructure provisioning and management using tools like Terraform, Ansible and Helm.

- Automate the deployment of applications, configurations and infrastructure to achieve a high level of flexibility and confidence in production setups and deployment processes.

- Improve our global security, challenge our worldwide scaling, increase our performance.

Within 6 months, you will: 

- Collaborate with other squads to implement and improve our DevOps practices.

- Monitor system performance, troubleshoot issues, and implement solutions to improve system stability and availability.

- Manage and maintain our Azure cloud infrastructure.

- Ensure the security and compliance of our systems and data.

- Participate in on-call rotations to provide 24/7 support.

- Manage incidents and post-mortem.

- Work closely with developers to facilitate their daily tasks, help them conform to best practices and ensure environments meet requirements (e.g.: simplify and automate the deployment process, provide metrics and monitoring to the engineering squads).

- Build and improve our internal platform: easy-to-deploy tools and templates that move infrastructure work off the squads' plate ("shift down"), so developers can ship without being infrastructure experts.

- Improve monitoring and load testing to secure and enhance the performance of our infrastructure

Within 12 months, you will: 

- Actively participate in DevOps decisions for all critical projects related to our platform’s performance and reliability.

- Evangelize and train our R&D team on Devops culture by defining all best practices and building them into the platform by default.

The Skill Set 

- 3+ years of experience as a DevOps Engineer or in a similar role.

- Ideally, you have worked in a tech or a SaaS company

- You know how to run systems in production

- Interest in platform engineering and developer experience: you like building tools that other engineers enjoy using

- Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, GitOps).

- Experience with containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

- Strong understanding of networking, security, and system administration.

- You have a coding background (scripting, programming)

- Passion for automation and continuous improvement.

- You have working proficiency in English (level B2 or equivalent)Fluent English (US/UK) / B2 level or equivalent (FR)

- Enthusiasm for our working environment explained here: https://bit.ly/Convexity_360L 

Our technical stack 

- 
Cloud: Azure Cloud

- 
Container orchestration: k8s, ArgoCD

- 
Infra as Code: Terraform, AnsibleHelm

- 
Monitoring tool: Datadog

- 
Database: MongoDB Atlas

- 
Application language: Javascript

What we offer: 

- Compensation: Package includes base salary, a variable component and equity 📈

- Benefits/Perks : Work From Home stipend, RTT, lunch vouchers, medical insurance, gym subscription, 1 month parental leave for the second parent. 

- Balance: Flexible hours, full remote work possible anywhere in France 🏠

- Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion : We have 6 active ERGs including Mental Health, Environmental/Sustainability, Women, Parents, LGBTQIA2S+, and Ethnic Diversity. Each group has at least one executive team member serving as a member of the group, bringing greater awareness to each group’s activities and providing a quick path to impact 🤝

- Corporate Social Responsibility : Review our CSR Charter: 360learning.com/blog/corporate-social-responsibility-charter 🌎🌏🌍

- Culture: A framework that will help you make an impact - envision our way of working and our Convexity Culture: https://bit.ly/Convexity_360L & find out more about the teams, product and processes https://bit.ly/42H1ggC 🚀👩🏻‍💻🏆

Interview Process:

- Discovery Meeting with our Lead Devops Engineer

- Case Study to do at home and to discuss with a Devops Engineer

- Clarification Meeting with a Devops Engineer

Who We Are 

360Learning enables companies to upskill from within by turning their experts into champions for employee, customer, and partner growth. With our LMS for collaborative learning, Learning & Development teams can accelerate upskilling with the help of internal experts instead of slow top-down training. 360Learning is the easiest way to onboard and upskill employees, train customer-facing teams, and enable customers and partners–all from one place.

title: Conseiller(ère) commercial(e) terrain expérimenté(e) Freelance
description:
Conseiller(ère) commercial(e) terrain expérimenté(e) 

Indépendant | Rémunération à la commission uniquement | Territoire de vente local | Commissions déplafonnées

À propos de l'opportunité

Nous recherchons des commerciaux terrain expérimentés, à l'aise pour se rendre dans une entreprise, engager la conversation avec le propriétaire et convaincre de nouveaux commerçants.

En tant que conseiller commercial itinérant indépendant, vous vendrez les solutions de paiement, de point de vente et logicielles de SumUp aux petites et moyennes entreprises de votre région. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d'opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route.

Vous devrez justifier d'une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.

Vos missions

- 
Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.

- 
Cibler les entreprises locales générant d'importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.

- 
Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels.

- 
Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat.

- 
Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp.

- 
Établir des relations avec les chefs d'entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits.

- 
Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d'optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.

- 
Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes.

- 
Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.

Ce que nous recherchons

Indispensable

- 
Au moins un an d'expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l'énergie, les technologies d'entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l'approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.

- 
Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects.

- 
Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.

- 
Des résultats démontrables en matière d'acquisition de nouveaux clients et d'atteinte d'objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu.

- 
La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections.

- 
Un bon sens de l'organisation et un suivi rigoureux.

- 
La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d'expérience et à persévérer.

- 
Une bonne compréhension du statut d'indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients.

- 
La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients.

Atouts

- 
Un réseau existant de chefs d'entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp.

- 
Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente.

Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain.

Rémunération

Il s'agit d'une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l'activité des commerçants apportés.

Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner :

- 
Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions.

- 
Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème.

- 
Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème.

- 
Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans.

- 
Avantage de bienvenue : trois fois le montant habituel des commissions résiduelles pendant les trois premiers mois.

- 
Primes supplémentaires liées à certains produits ou opérations commerciales.

Les nouveaux partenaires bénéficient des conditions Partner pendant la période de lancement. Leur maintien est ensuite soumis aux critères d'activité du programme ; un barème Agent de 40 %, sans commissions résiduelles, peut s'appliquer.

Les conditions d'éligibilité, les bases de calcul et les modalités de versement sont précisées dans le contrat et présentées avant tout engagement. Les commissions s'entendent avant déduction de vos frais professionnels, cotisations sociales et impôts applicables.

Nous vous aiderons à vous familiariser avec les produits et leur commercialisation grâce à un parcours initial et à un accompagnement continu couvrant la prospection, les entretiens de vente, les démonstrations, la gestion des objections et l'accompagnement des clients.

Les modalités du parcours initial et les prérequis à la commercialisation vous seront communiqués avant le démarrage.

Votre interlocuteur SumUp vous apportera également son soutien en matière de développement territorial, d'analyse de vos opportunités et de conseils commerciaux, dans le respect de votre autonomie d'organisation.

title: Sales Development Representative - CDI
description:
Qui sommes-nous ? 

Notre mission 

Avec Solteo, nous voulons donner toutes ses chances à l'électrification des bâtiments en soutenant ceux qui sont en première ligne : les entreprises d’installation. 

⚡ Produire son électricité en solaire, se chauffer avec une pompe à chaleur, recharger son véhicule, stocker : l'électrification des bâtiments est le premier levier de décarbonation . Le photovoltaïque ouvre la marche — selon Xavier Piechaczyk de RTE : “le photovoltaïque a un grand potentiel, mais il faut accélérer rapidement” 

👷‍♂️ La disponibilité des installateurs freine cette accélération. Ces professionnels limités en nombre perdent souvent du temps sur l'organisation et la gestion de projets de plus en plus techniques. Rien qu'en solaire, ils ont 4M de foyers à équiper d'ici 2030 !

💻 Solteo est la plateforme d'organisation de projets d’électrification qui aide les installateurs à gérer leur temps et leurs projets, quel que soit l'équipement posé. Nos premières métriques : 75% de temps gagné, +30% de conversion, et des utilisateurs heureux ! 

Le mot de la CEO 

“Entreprendre est le moyen le plus efficace d’avoir un impact ! C'est pour cela que nous avons choisi le secteur de l'énergie, et plus particulièrement celui de l’électrification. Nous façonnons le monde de demain, celui de la décentralisation des énergies renouvelables : pas à pas, projet par projet. Nous accélérons cette transition et surtout, nous la rendons possible. Ce qui est sûr, c'est que nous nous sentons utiles, notre produit plaît et devient rapidement indispensable chez nos utilisateurs.
Rejoindre Solteo, c’est savoir écouter et rester attentif aux retours de nos clients et de notre marché, car ce sont eux qui façonnent la trajectoire de Solteo ! Ce produit, c’est avant tout le leur !” — Manon

Et ce poste alors ? 

Le rôle 

En première ligne de notre développement commercial , tu travailleras main dans la main avec le Sales Manager et les Account Executives au sein d'une équipe outillée et ambitieuse, sur un cycle de vente court.

Missions et responsabilités 

- Prospection intensive et ciblée (Outbound) : Identifier et qualifier des comptes clés dans le secteur de l'installation solaire. Tu contacteras les prospects via une approche multicanale avec une majorité de Cold Calling (notre cible d'artisans est très réceptive au téléphone), du Cold Emailing et LinkedIn.

- Qualification des leads (Inbound & Outbound) : Traiter rapidement les demandes entrantes générées par le marketing. Tu devras qualifier les besoins lors des premiers appels de découverte et transformer l'intérêt en rendez-vous de démonstration qualifié pour l'équipe de closing.

- Rigueur opérationnelle et Data : Assurer une tenue irréprochable de notre CRM (HubSpot) via la mise à jour des statuts, la prise de notes et le log des appels. Tu utiliseras notre stack et suivras tes KPIs quotidiens et hebdomadaires.

- Amélioration continue : Remonter les objections fréquentes et les retours du terrain au VP Sales et au Marketing pour affiner le discours. Tu participeras activement aux sessions de coaching et de partage de bonnes pratiques de l'équipe.

Tes objectifs: 

⭐ 0 à 1 mois : L'onboarding et les premiers pas 
Acquérir une compréhension parfaite du produit Solteo, de la proposition de valeur et du marché cible. Prendre en main la stack technique (HubSpot, Aircall, Apollo) et lancer tes premières séquences de prospection et appels à froid pour générer tes premiers SQL.
🎯 Objectif : Maîtrise du pitch commercial, des outils de prospection et autonomie dans la génération de rendez-vous.

⭐ 1 à 8 mois : L'exécution et la machine à leads 
Exécuter les séquences avec régularité et intensité. Atteindre et dépasser tes quotas de rendez-vous bookés. Devenir une machine de qualification tout en encaissant les refus sans perdre ta motivation.
🎯 Objectif : Alimenter continuellement les agendas des Account Executives avec des leads ultra-qualifiés.

⭐ À partir de 8 mois : Les premières démos (Closing) 
C'est la concrétisation de ta montée en compétences ! Tu ne fais plus que prospecter : tu commences à prendre le relais sur la suite du cycle de vente en réalisant tes premières démonstrations produit auprès des prospects que tu as qualifiés.
🎯 Objectif : Maîtriser l'exercice de la démo et initier ta transition vers le closing.

⭐ >1 an : L'évolution 
Participer à l'amélioration des process de prospection et transmettre ton savoir aux nouveaux arrivants.
🎯 Objectif : Évoluer officiellement vers un poste d'Account Executive (Closer) à temps plein ou prendre des responsabilités managériales au sein de l'équipe SDR.

Les compétences qu’on recherche 

- Formation : Tu as une expérience dans la vente SaaS B2B !

- Mindset : Tu as un mindset d'entrepreneur, tu aimes relever des challenges et mettre la main à la pâte.

- Humilité et capacité à se remettre en question : Forte envie de progresser et de prendre des responsabilités.

- Langues : Français et Anglais parfaitement bilingues/fluents.

Ce qui serait un plus 

- Une expérience dans la Construction Tech ou l' Energy Tech , ou auprès des artisans et du bâtiment.

- Une réelle motivation pour les projets à impact et la transition énergétique.

Mais Solteo c’est aussi… 

- Un cadre professionnel vivant et énergique, où la prise d’initiatives est non seulement appréciée mais également récompensée.

- La chance de parfaire et d'enrichir tes connaissances dans un secteur en pleine croissance et qui a du sens.

- Des bureaux situés en plein centre de Paris, avec plusieurs autres start-ups du solaire

- Une diversité de projets captivants, offrant l'opportunité de collaborer avec des clients diverses et variés. Pas possible de s’ennuyer !

description:

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Embedded Engineer, you will own the firmware that runs on that hardware, from the first register write to the moment data leaves the device, so that what reaches our ML team is clean, synchronized, and trustworthy.

What You Will Do 

- Write and own the firmware for our data-capture hardware: sensors, motion-capture rigs, custom IoT setups, and prototype robots.

- Build real-time data acquisition: drivers, DMA, buffering, and streaming from many sensors at once without dropping a sample.

- Solve multi-sensor synchronization, calibration, and time-stamping so every data point lines up across devices and modalities.

- Bring up new boards with our Electrical Engineer and turn fresh hardware into working devices fast.

- Build the path from device to dataset: communication protocols, on-device logging, and handoff into our data pipeline.

- Work shoulder to shoulder with ML engineers. Your firmware decides what their training data looks like, and a timing bug can quietly ruin months of data.

- Make firmware reliable in the field: testing, OTA updates, error handling, and diagnostics that tell us what went wrong.

Requirements 

- Up to 5 years writing production firmware for embedded or IoT systems.

- Strong C/C++, experience with an RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar), and deep familiarity with microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar).

- Hands-on experience with peripheral interfaces and protocols: SPI, I2C, UART, USB, BLE, CAN, or similar.

- Experience integrating sensors in firmware: IMUs, cameras, depth sensors, force sensors, or similar.

- A strong understanding of how firmware decisions affect data quality, especially for EMG/EEG sensing: ADC configuration, sample rate, jitter, filtering, and buffering. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you write code accordingly.

- Comfortable debugging at the hardware boundary with a logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and debugger.

- Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice.

- High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. You are comfortable in 0-to-1 ambiguity, where the spec is "figure out what the spec should be".

- Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care.

- Fluent in English. German is a plus.

Nice to Have 

- A background in robotics, motion capture, or wearable devices.

title: Embedded Control Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE 

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO 

- Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

- Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

- Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT 

In this role, you will play a key part in developing the embedded control platform and will translate functional and control requirements into embedded hardware and software architectures, select appropriate microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA, or other controller technologies, and develop real-time software close to the hardware implementation. Your work will directly influence the performance, reliability, safety, and will require close collaboration with power electronics, integrated electronics, mechanical, thermal, and system engineers.

WHAT YOU WILL DO 

- Define embedded controller architectures for power electronic converters and select suitable microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA.

- Translate power electronics and control requirements into efficient, deterministic, and robust real-time software implementations.

- Develop, test, debug, and validate embedded software on target hardware, from individual software blocks through complete controller implementations and automated testing environments to validate the design.

- Explore new controller technologies, embedded architectures, and software implementation concepts to improve converter performance, flexibility, reliability, functionality, and maintainability.

WHO YOU ARE 

- You hold a University (Higher education) degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- You have a strong understanding of embedded architectures, and the practical considerations involved in selecting controllers for demanding real-time applications.

- You are an expert in embedded software development for real-time applications, preferably in power electronics, industrial automation, or similar applications, spanning FPGA programming, systems programming, hardware interfaces and communication protocols.

- You are experienced in monitoring and debugging software directly on target hardware

NICE TO HAVE 

- Experience with model-based development, hardware-in-the-loop testing, automated testing, or safety-critical software development is a plus.

INTERVIEW PROCESS 

- Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

- Technical Screening (30 min)

- Technical Panel (3x60 min)

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

We're looking for an experienced partnerships leader to build and scale ElevenLabs' Public Sector Partner Programme in North America — bringing together resellers, VARs, and systems integrators who help deploy our technology across federal agencies, state and local governments, and education institutions.

You'll own the public sector partner strategy end-to-end — from building relationships with leading SIs and VARs with established public sector practices, to onboarding, enabling, and activating them to sell and deliver ElevenLabs products into government and education accounts.

Requirements

- Written communication: Excellent technical writing skills and the ability to explain complex scientific concepts clearly, precisely, and logically.

title: Senior Structural Assembly Manufacturing Engineer
description:
About Electra 

Air travel is about to become something more: more direct, more accessible, and more connected to the places where people live, work and want to be. Every day in the U.S., people make 35 million trips of 50–500 miles, stuck in traffic or routed through crowded hubs. Chances are, you've been one of them. At Electra, we're changing that with the EL9, a nine-passenger, hybrid-electric aircraft that takes off and lands in just 150 feet. Our Ultra Short technology opens up thousands of new places to fly, beyond conventional runways, congested airports and long drives. We're backed by Lockheed Martin, Honeywell and Safran. Operators worldwide have signed intent-to-purchase agreements for the first 2,200 aircraft we produce, and we're moving toward first test flights in 2027. 

Getting a new kind of aircraft airborne takes more than ambition. It takes our kind of bold: people who think big while working in the real world. Who move ideas into action and collaborate without silos. Who put people first and make room at the table for everyone. Who challenge one another without diminishing one another. 

Sound like you? Then look beyond what you thought were your own limits, and help us take flight beyond runways. 

The Role 

As Electra's Senior Structural Assembly Manufacturing Engineer, you'll play a key role in developing and industrializing the structural assembly processes for the EL9 aircraft, working from early product development through prototype build, production implementation, and ramp-up.

You'll work closely with Product Engineering during aircraft development to ensure structural designs incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and can be efficiently, repeatably, and reliably produced. You'll bring a hands-on manufacturing perspective to structural design decisions, evaluating assembly sequence, tolerance management, access, tooling, fastening and joining methods, inspection requirements, producibility, and production risk.

As the EL9 transitions from design into physical hardware, you'll help translate released engineering into executable manufacturing processes and support prototype and initial aircraft builds. You'll work closely with airframe manufacturing suppliers, providing on-site Manufacturing Engineering oversight and liaison support as needed to ensure proper information flow, resolve technical and quality issues, support the incorporation of product changes and support supply chain on contract management.

This is an opportunity to influence both how the aircraft is designed and how it is ultimately built, while helping establish Electra's structural assembly manufacturing supply chain capability from the ground up.

What You'll Do 

- Partner with Product Engineering throughout aircraft development to ensure structural designs incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and support efficient, repeatable, and scalable production.

- Review aircraft structural designs, assemblies, drawings, models, and engineering changes from a manufacturing perspective, providing recommendations related to producibility, assembly sequence, access, tolerance stack-up, fastening and joining methods, tooling, inspection, and production risk.

- Participate in design trade studies, concept reviews, and design reviews, representing Manufacturing Engineering and identifying manufacturing constraints and opportunities early in the development cycle.

- Provide Manufacturing Engineering oversight and liaison support at airframe and structural suppliers, working directly with supplier manufacturing teams to clarify design and manufacturing intent, resolve producibility and assembly issues, and maintain program execution.

- Work closely with the airframe supplier Tooling Engineering to define assembly tooling concepts, requirements, locating strategies, interfaces, and implementation plans.

- Review supplier manufacturing approaches, build plans, assembly processes, tooling concepts, and production readiness to ensure alignment with Electra's engineering requirements and program objectives.

- Support prototype fabrication, development aircraft assembly, first builds, and production implementation, providing hands-on Manufacturing Engineering support to resolve issues encountered during structural assembly.

- Coordinate technical resolution of manufacturing issues and nonconformances with Product Engineering, Stress, Quality, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders.

- Capture manufacturing lessons learned and supplier feedback from prototype and initial production builds and drive those learnings back into product design, manufacturing processes, tooling, and planning.

- Support structural assembly production ramp-up by identifying constraints, resolving manufacturing issues, improving assembly processes, and driving improvements in quality, cost, schedule, and production rate.

- Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of Electra manufacturing engineering standards, methods, processes, and best practices.

What You Bring 

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Aeronautical, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering field.

- 8+ years of aerospace manufacturing engineering experience, with significant experience in aircraft structural assembly and industrialization.

- Strong hands-on knowledge of aircraft structural assembly processes, including metallic and/or composite airframe structures, drilling, fastening, joining, shimming, sealing, alignment, and major structural integration.

- Demonstrated experience applying Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles during aircraft product development.

- Experience reviewing engineering drawings, 3D models, GD&T, tolerances, and engineering changes from a manufacturing and assembly perspective.

- Experience developing manufacturing plans, assembly sequences, work instructions, tooling requirements, and manufacturing engineering documentation.

- Experience supporting prototype, development, or first-production aircraft builds.

- Experience working directly with aircraft structures suppliers or manufacturing partners and supporting production activities in a factory environment.

- Demonstrated ability to work effectively across Product Engineering, Stress, Quality, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, Tooling, and Production organizations.

- Strong problem-solving skills and ability to make sound engineering recommendations in a fast-moving aircraft development environment.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across internal teams and external suppliers.

- Ability and willingness to travel to supplier and manufacturing locations as required by program needs.

Bonus Points 

- Experience with clean-sheet aircraft development and transition from prototype into production.

- Experience with major structural assemblies such as fuselage, wing, empennage, control surfaces, or other primary airframe structures.

- Experience with aircraft assembly tooling, jigs, fixtures, determinant assembly, or advanced assembly methodologies.

- Experience with digital manufacturing tools, PLM/MES environments, manufacturing BOMs, and 3D model-based manufacturing.

- Experience with supplier industrialization, production readiness assessments, or manufacturing capability reviews.

- Experience with MRB, root cause corrective action, and production nonconformance resolution.

- Experience with AS9100 aerospace quality management systems.

This range reflects the anticipated hiring range across all eligible locations; actual compensation is determined based on your relevant experience, skills, and geographic location. Total compensation includes performance bonus and comprehensive benefits.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
description:
SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories — the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed. 

Every part we make generates data, decisions, and handoffs. Your job is to capture that knowledge, automate the work around it, and remove whatever slows production down. When a critical defense program needs parts by next week, the systems you build are why we can deliver. 

The Role As a Full-Stack Software Engineer on our manufacturing intelligence team, you'll work wherever the leverage is highest. One week that means turning an operator's spreadsheet into a proper workflow; the next it means wiring machine data into scheduling, or cutting a manual quoting step out of the order flow. 

You'll own problems end to end across our customer portal, Enterprise Resource Planning / Manufacturing Execution System, and the data layer connecting them to the shop floor. 

Based at our HQ at “The Circle” (Zurich airport), your work will span: 

- Manufacturing Intelligence: Capturing process, machine, and quality data so knowledge lives in systems instead of in people's heads. 

- Automation: Replacing manual steps in quoting, planning, scheduling, and documentation with software that runs on its own. 

- Production Acceleration: Finding the bottlenecks between CAD/CAM data submission and shipped parts. 

- Tools for People: Building interfaces that make life easier for operators, engineers, and customers, whether that's a work instruction screen, a dashboard, or a self-service portal. 

Importantly, you do not need prior experience in the manufacturing domain. We value a high level of curiosity and autonomy to find and solve problems. 

What We're Looking For - Experience: 3+ years as a software engineer with proven experience in shipping code to production, across backend and frontend 

- Broad Technical Range: Experience in systems design, architecture and implementation. In general, you don’t shy away from new technologies and pick up whatever the problem requires. Our current tech stack is: Rust, PostgreSQL, React, Python, AWS.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description:
Join us in building the ultimate online playground! 

Poki is on a mission to create the ultimate online playground, bringing easy access to the best games on web to over 100 million monthly players worldwide. These games are created by a dynamic global community of 500+ game developer teams. At the core of our work lies a simple belief: play is how we learn. This value is embodied by our team of 70 unique individuals who each bring something special to the table.

What this job is about 

As a senior Frontend Developer at Poki, you'll shape how players experience our platform. All the way from the first vague problem to what happens after release. That might mean improving discovery on a slow connection, running an experiment, building a tool for our Content team, or fixing a part of the stack everyone has quietly learned to work around.

This is a senior role. That means we're looking for judgement, not just throughput.

Your Challenge as a senior Frontend Developer 

- Frontend that works on real devices. That means a three-year-old Android phone on unreliable wifi, not just the MacBook that will run anything you throw at it. If it only feels smooth on your machine, it is not done.

- Clear work from vague problems. You turn "players are leaving on slow connections" into a sensible scope, a first slice and a clear opinion about what can wait.

- Results you can point at. Decide what success looks like before you build, then use A/B tests and our data to see if you got there. If nothing moves, say so. Sometimes the right result is killing the thing you just built.

- Ownership in production. You build in enough monitoring to know when your work breaks, then stay with it until it is fixed. Shipping is the start of ownership, not the end.

- A stronger engineering team. Your reviews teach, your pairing unblocks people and the patterns you leave behind make the next piece of work easier.

- A stack and a codebase that survive contact with other people. You understand what still earns its place, what is hanging around through habit, and when changing it is worth the cost. What you leave behind, code and reasoning both, still makes sense six months later when the context is gone and somebody else needs to change it.

- Visible progress in small slices. Something useful in a week beats something theoretically perfect in two months. It also tells you much sooner when the idea was wrong.

You 

- Ownership of the whole scope, judgement before throughput. That includes the awkward parts that nobody volunteered for. The goal is not to produce more code, it is to build the right thing.

- Strong, production-level experience with React, Redux, TypeScript, HTML and CSS (7+ years). You've shipped and maintained SPAs at scale, not just built one from a tutorial, and you know where the codebase tends to rot if nobody's watching.

- Write tests with a reason . Use Playwright or something similar where it catches real problems, not because a coverage number looks better.

- Use AI to move faster while keeping the judgment, understanding and outcome yours. You do not ship something you cannot explain.

- Build something small and measure it. That turns gut feeling into evidence and shows which ideas deserve to become real features.

- Disagree properly, then commit . Make the case early and explain the tradeoffs in terms engineers and non-engineers can understand. Once the call is made you are in, including when it went the other way.

- Are familiar with Figma or a similar tool, and are comfortable translating designs into interactive web components.

title: Quality Officer
description:
Bij Crisp willen we beter eten mogelijk maken voor meer mensen. Dat begint met eten waar je op kunt vertrouwen: veilig, hygiënisch en elke keer net zo goed als we beloven. Daarom zorg jij ervoor dat kwaliteit, hygiëne en voedselveiligheid op de productievloer elke dag kloppen. Je bent onze ogen en oren op de vloer. Het fundament staat als een huis: HACCP, kwaliteit en specificatiebeheer zijn op orde. Jij zorgt dat de praktijk daar dagelijks bij aansluit en je stuurt bij waar het nodig is. Je bent veel op de productievloer te vinden voor controles en om processen te verifiëren. Af en toe zit je in ons eigen lab voor experimenten en testen.

Wat deze rol zo leuk maakt? Je hebt direct invloed op ons product en je zit er altijd dichtbij. Schuurt het ergens op kwaliteit, dan ben jij het aanspreekpunt voor de productie. Klachten pak je grondig op en je zoekt praktische oplossingen.

Wat je gaat doen

- Je loopt dagelijks kwaliteits- en hygiënerondes op de productievloer. Je controleert of collega’s de werkwijzen en kwaliteitsstandaarden naleven.

- Je neemt monsters en doet snelle producttesten en metingen, zoals pH en temperatuur. Ook controleer je inkomende grondstoffen en inkoopartikelen.

- Je voert gerichte controle- en testprogramma’s uit op smaak, microbiologie, chemie, fysieke eigenschappen en allergenen, bij processen, grondstoffen en eindproducten.

- Je coördineert en interpreteert laboratoriumonderzoeken (M/C/F/A) en voert houdbaarheidsstudies uit.

- Je coördineert en zet smaaktesten en proeverijen in.

- Je onderzoekt klachten van klanten over producten grondig. Je duikt de productie in, achterhaalt waar het misging en borgt de oplossing.

- Je let op de juiste toepassing van onze vaste productspecificaties en etiketteringseisen tijdens de productie.

- Je controleert, test en kalibreert meet- en weegapparatuur.

- Je spreekt productiemedewerkers aan, coacht ze en geeft korte, praktische trainingen en instructies, bijvoorbeeld over hygiëne en allergenen. Zo tillen we de voedselveiligheidscultuur elke dag naar een hoger niveau.

- Afhankelijk van je ambities en ervaring is er ruimte om mee te denken over productontwikkeling, bezoek je leveranciers om grondstoffen aan de bron te toetsen, help je bij inkoop en hygiënemanagement en ondersteun je bij kwaliteit in warehouse en logistiek.

Dit ben jij

- Je bent praktisch en zichtbaar. Je zit niet graag hele dagen achter een bureau. Jij bent op je best op de productievloer.

- Je bent een goede communicator en coach. Je legt kwaliteitsregels helder uit en spreekt collega’s op een prettige, opbouwende manier aan als iemand zich er niet aan houdt.

- Je bent kritisch en nauwkeurig. Je let op details, kijkt scherp naar het proces en neemt geen genoegen met half werk.

- Je bent zelfredzaam en oplossingsgericht. Je pakt zaken zelf op, weet bij wie je moet zijn en komt je afspraken na.

- Je bent flexibel. Loopt je dag op de vloer anders door een kwaliteitsprobleem of een urgente klacht? Dan schakel je snel en pas je je prioriteiten aan.

- Je hebt minimaal MBO+/HBO werk- en denkniveau.

- Je hebt gedegen basiskennis van levensmiddelen (microbiologie, chemie en allergenen). Je weet hoe kruisbesmetting werkt en kunt labuitslagen interpreteren.

- Je kent de basis van HACCP, de hygiënecode, algemene warenwetgeving en GFSI-normen, zoals BRCGS, IFS of FSSC 22000.

- Pre: een opleiding in Levensmiddelentechnologie, Voedingskunde of een vergelijkbare richting.

- Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem.

Damit sitzt du an der Stelle im Unternehmen, an der beide Seiten gleichzeitig sichtbar sind : Du weißt, was Kunden wirklich brauchen und wofür sie zahlen — und du weißt, was das Produkt kann und was es kosten würde, es zu können. Du bist die erste Person in dieser Rolle und baust den Bereich so, wie er in zwei Jahren für dreißig Leute funktionieren muss.

Nopan is a payment performance platform built by former merchants, focused exclusively on account and wallet payment methods. In just 18 months, we secured our license from the Dutch Central Bank, formed partnerships with Europe's major payment schemes, including becoming a Principal Member of EPI/Wero, and went live with initial customers. - Endless opportunities for professional growth as the company scales.

title: Director, Experience Intelligence and Quality
description:
Our mission: eliminating every barrier to mental health. 

Spring Health is a global mental health company on a mission to eliminate every barrier to mental health. We're building a world where getting support is simple, personal, and built around the person, so care can continue through every job, move, health plan, and life stage.

Our AI-native platform helps us deliver personalized support across self-guided tools, coaching, therapy, medication management, and specialty care. With outcomes independently validated by JAMA Network Open and the Validation Institute, Spring Health reaches more than 170 million people worldwide through leading employers, health plans, and partners.

As an AI-native company, we believe technology should expand the reach, quality, and humanity of care. Every Spring Health team member is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully, apply human judgment to AI outputs, and keep building AI fluency in ways that support their role and our mission.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Care Operations Intelligence, the Director, Experience Intelligence & Quality owns the voice-of-customer (VoC) signal infrastructure that captures what Spring Health’s members, providers, employers, and payers are experiencing. Additionally, this leader will own the standards our frontline support and clinical teams are measured against: QA methodology, rubrics, calibration, and improvement strategy across every channel. This role will be responsible for continuing to shift the VoC and quality teams into an AI native organization. This is a full time, fully-remote position, though the ability to be onsite in our NYC office once a week is preferred.

What you’ll do: 

- Build and run the voice-of-customer / signal-synthesis capability: consolidate unstructured member, provider, employer, and payer feedback into a single signal infrastructure. Insights Ops teams can act on directly go to QA, Training, and function owners; systemic issues needing product, policy, or process change get surfaced to Process Engineering, Product, and other cross-functional partners.

- Own an AI-native cross-channel quality strategy: one measurement standard, one defect taxonomy, one sampling approach, and one calibration process spanning AI-handled and human-handled interactions.

- Partner with Process Engineering on the diagnose/fix boundary: this role sets the QA rubric and methodology that AI-failure diagnoses are scored against; day-to-day gap-log triage sits with Process Engineering pending the working-session decision on scope.

- Design a signal- and defect-prioritization framework so the highest-impact issues get worked first, partnering with frontline leadership to design and evaluate quality improvement initiatives (e.g., training updates, workflow changes, automation opportunities).

- Own the tool stack used across VoC and QA, including consolidating vendors where possible.

- Build out and manage a high-leverage team spanning all elements of the quality and VoC cycle: VoC analysts, quality strategists, and QA reviewers led by a Senior Manager.

What success looks like: 

- A working VoC signal pipeline — feedback synthesized, prioritized, and routed — with a measurable VoC-driven action rate and shrinking insight-to-action cycle time.

- One quality measurement standard and defect taxonomy in place across AI and human channels, replacing two divergent stacks.

- QA coverage of support and clinical interactions increasing via automation, with calibration variance and inter-rater agreement inside range.

- Reliable critical-error (compliance/HIPAA) catch rates.

- Leadership and cross-functional partners have a trusted, evidence-based read on where quality is breaking and why, across AI and human-delivered service alike.

- CSAT trending up across member, provider, employer, and payer groups.

What you’ll bring: 

- 8+ years of experience in operations strategy, analytics, or a related role (e.g., management consulting), preferably within healthcare; 5+ years in a leadership role.

- Experience running voice-of-customer or signal-management programs and turning unstructured feedback into prioritized, actionable insight.

- Experience leading quality functions in a high-volume service delivery environment (healthcare, contact center, or similar).

- Demonstrated ability to partner with senior executives to solve complex business challenges using data, structured analysis, and exceptional communication skills.

- Track record integrating two teams or tools into one operating model (post-acquisition or post-reorg) without stalling either program mid-transition.

- A builder’s mindset — comfortable establishing frameworks, processes, and standards in a scaling environment.

- People leadership experience managing managers or multiple sub-functions.

Nice to have: 

- Direct experience building or scaling a QA function — scoring rubrics, calibration programs, inter-rater reliability — ideally including a shift from manual/sampling review toward AI-assisted or AI-native scoring.

- Experience with AI-scoring / auto-QA platforms (e.g., Zendesk QA, Maestro QA or similar).

- Background spanning both care/clinical delivery and RCM, claims, or another regulated, financial-services-adjacent operations environment.

- Comfort operating with real ambiguity — this org is still being designed as part of an active M&A integration, and several ownership boundaries with Process Engineering aren't finalized yet.

Benefits provided by Spring Health: 

Note : We have even more benefits than listed here and below, your recruiter will provide more in-depth information as you continue in the interview process. Benefits are subject to individual plan requirements and eligibility criteria. 

- Health, Dental, Vision benefits start on your first day at Spring. You and your dependents also receive access to One Medical accounts HSA and FSA plans are also available, with Spring contributing up to $1K for HSAs, depending on your plan type.

- Employer sponsored 401(k) match of up to 2% for retirement planning

- A yearly allotment of no cost visits to the Spring Health network of therapists, coaches, and medication management providers for you and your dependents.

- We offer competitive paid time off policies including vacation, sick leave and company holidays.

- At 6 months tenure with Spring, we offer parental leave of 18 weeks for birthing parents and 16 weeks for non-birthing parents.

- Access to Noom , a weight management program—based in psychology, that’s tailored to your unique needs and goals. 

- Access to fertility care support through Carrot , in addition to $4,000 reimbursement for related fertility expenses.

- Access to Wellhub , which connects employees to the best options for fitness, mindfulness, nutrition, and sleep in one subscription

- Access to BrightHorizons , which provides sponsored child care, back-up care, and elder care

- Up to $1,000 Professional Development Reimbursement a year.

- $200 per year donation matching to support your favorite causes.

Not sure if you meet every requirement? Research shows that women and people from historically underrepresented communities often hesitate to apply for roles unless they meet every qualification compared to other similarly-qualified candidates. At Spring Health, we are committed to fostering a workplace where everyone feels valued, empowered, and supported to Thrive . If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply.

We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable legal requirements. Spring Health is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

Wir wissen, dass unsere Produkte im deutschen Markt funktionieren. Daher heißt es jetzt: wachsen, wachsen, wachsen. Gleichzeitig gibt es einige länderspezifische Anforderungen zu beachten. Gemeinsam mit dem Betriebsführer / Meister und dem Installationsplaner bildest du eine starke Einheit, die durch deine technische Expertise, Serviceorientierung und eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten geprägt ist.

Wir legen großen Wert auf kurze Wege, digitale Prozesse, direkte Kommunikation, schnelle Entscheidungsprozesse und Spaß an der Arbeit mit motivierenden Incentives.

Täglich befasst du dich mit: 

- Betriebsleitung der deutschen GmbH

- Führung des operativen Teams

- Training unserer Installationspartner

- Technische/r Experte/in für alle installationsbedingten Fragestellungen

- After-Sales Service sowie ausstehenden Reparaturen oder Inbetriebnahmen unserer Wärmepumpen in der NRW Region

- Durchführung von Installationen unserer Wärmepumpe zusammen mit dem Installationsteam

- Behebung von Störungen, die das Serviceteam nicht aus der Ferne beheben konnte

Warum Techniker bei uns bleiben

Unser Serviceteam im Büro löst etwa neun von zehn Meldungen aus der Ferne und plant deine Woche. Du fährst zu den Kunden, bei denen wirklich jemand vorbeikommen muss. Du bekommst um acht Uhr abends keinen Anruf. Da wir das Produkt selbst herstellen, werden die Erkenntnisse, die du vor Ort sammelst, direkt an die Ingenieure weitergeleitet. Du behebst nicht nur Störungen, sondern sorgst dafür, dass sie beim nächsten Mal nicht mehr auftreten.

Du arbeitest selbstständig und bis größtenteils beim Kunden vor Ort und hast gleichzeitig deine Base in unserem Büro in Düsseldorf, wo du dich regelmäßig mit dem Team vernetzen kannst.

Dein Profil

Berufserfahrung:

- Meister im Bereich SHK oder vergleichbare Qualifikation

- Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Installation von Wärmepumpen

- Erfahrung in der Führung von Teams

- Mind. fünfjährige relevante Berufserfahrung

- Idealerweise Ausbildung/ Weiterbildung im Bereich Elektrotechnik

- Hands-on-Mentalität, ausgeprägte Eigeninitiative

- Lösungs- und Serviceorientierung

- Zuverlässige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise

Sprache:

- Deutsch (fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse)

- Englisch (mind. Grundkenntnisse)

Zusatzqualifikation/Zertifikat:

- PKW Führerschein (Erforderlich)

- Idealerweise abgeschlossene TRGI und/ oder TRWI Schulung

Arbeitsort: Vor Ort beim Kunden in NRW, ca. 1-2 Tage die Woche im Düsseldorfer Büro

Unser Angebot

Als Mitglied bei DeWarmte im deutschen Markt hilfst du von Tag 1 uns als führende Marke zu etablieren. Dabei erhältst du volle Unterstützung aus unserem niederländischen und Düsseldorfer Büro sowie Anleitung von unserem erfahrenen Meister und arbeitest in einem motivierten, familiären Umfeld, in dem du einen echten Beitrag zur Energiewende leistest.

- 55.000 - 75.000 € Bruttojahresgehalt

- Unbefristete Anstellung mit Gestaltungsmöglichkeit in einem expandierenden Unternehmen

- Fahrtzeit ist bei uns Arbeitszeit

- Teilnahme an unserem Stock Appreciation Rights (SAR)-Programm – du profitierst als Co-Owner direkt vom Wachstum von DeWarmte

- 27 Urlaubstage;

- Einsatzplanung mind. 1 Woche im Voraus. Nur lokale Einsätze

- Firmenwagen auch zur privaten Nutzung

- Laptop/ Tablet und Mobiltelefon

- Hochwertiges Werkzeug und Arbeitskleidung

- Individuelles Budget für deine persönliche Weiterentwicklung

- Kostenlose Getränke und Parkplatz an unserem Standort in Düsseldorf

- Gutes Betriebsklima und ein respektvoller Umgang im Team

- Mitarbeiterrabatt

- Firmenevents

- Build our Northwest Arkansas talent pipeline from zero: schools, trade programs, local manufacturers, veteran networks, and community partners

- Can run hiring in two very different markets without either one feeling like the afterthought

Bonus Points

You get to build the hiring engine for a factory before it exists, at a company where manufacturing is the whole ballgame.

description:
