Read this part first

Somewhere out there is a sourcer who is better than their job title says they are. They hit their numbers at a company that never let them talk to a hiring manager. They found the candidate nobody else found and watched a recruiter take the credit. They have been told to be patient, to wait for the next cycle, to earn it.

We are not going to make you wait.

What we do

We build autonomous aircraft and Legion, the software that flies hundreds of them as one coordinated swarm. Series A, backed by Khosla Ventures, and Coatue. We are hiring software engineers and aircraft engineers at the same time, which is hard, and how fast we hire is one of the few things standing between the current aircraft and the next one.

That is not a motivational line. It is the actual constraint. Recruiting is on the critical path here, and you will be able to see your work in the flight schedule.

The job

You own top of funnel for our software engineering roles: backend, frontend, autonomy, forward deployed. You will be reading GitHub profiles, writing outreach that engineers answer, and building searches that keep producing after the obvious names are gone.

Then the interesting part. Inside your first year you move onto the aircraft side: propulsion, structures, avionics, manufacturing, production. Almost nobody sources both. The people who can are rare enough that it changes what your career looks like from that point forward. We will teach you, and you will be bad at it for a while, and then you will not be.

What you get here that you did not get there

- Your own reqs, early, with your name on the outcome

- Hiring managers in the same building, not behind an intake form

- The freedom to change the message when it is not working, without asking three people first

- Someone who runs sourcing searches themselves every day and will look at your search strings with you

- A skill set at the end of two years that maybe a few hundred people in the country have

What we need from you

- 1+ years of sourcing or recruiting, most of it in software engineering

- A hire you are proud of, one nobody else was going to find, and the ability to walk us through exactly how you found them

- A high tolerance for silence, because most of your outreach will go unanswered and the job is making the next message better anyway

- Real curiosity about how aircraft get built, or at least the honesty to say you find it interesting and want in

- Writing that sounds like a person, since your entire work product is text a stranger decides to open or delete

- Clean data habits, because our reporting goes to the CEO and it needs to be right

What we do not need

Ten years of experience. A recruiting pedigree. A degree in anything specific. Permission from your current manager to be good at this.

The honest version

The pace is uncomfortable. You will be asked to fill roles you do not understand yet, and the answer will usually be to go learn them rather than to wait for a briefing.

If you want a clear ladder and a quiet quarter, this is the wrong job. If you have been waiting for someone to hand you something real, this is the shot.

description:
About HappyRobot 

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate through voice and email - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across entire enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo with over $200M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

About the Role 
As a Customer Support Engineer , youʼll be on the front lines of our customer
experience. Youʼll work directly with customers to quickly triage issues, debug
problems, and ensure theyʼre getting the most out of HappyRobotʼs AI platform.

This role is a hybrid between technical support and customer engineering: youʼll
diagnose issues, design and test quick solutions, and collaborate closely with both
engineering and product teams to make our platform even stronger.

Youʼll also apply prompt engineering skills to help customers fine-tune their AI
workers, ensuring accuracy, reliability, and speed across real-world logistics
workflows.

This role is ideal for someone with strong technical fundamentals who wants to
grow into a more senior customer engineering or product-facing position over
time.

Tech Profile 

- Comfortable Full-Stack: Python, React, TypeScript, Node.js. 

- Experience managing APIs and integrations with third-party systems.

- Some exposure to infrastructure and cloud deployments.

- Familiarity with LLM prompting and tuning of voices/transcribers; eager to
experiment and iterate.

- Strong debugging and problem-solving skills — quick at identifying the root
cause of issues.

Must Have 

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English — able to explain
technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

- Strong ability to triage, prioritize, and resolve issues independently under
tight deadlines.

- Curiosity and adaptability: you can learn customer workflows quickly and
propose solutions.

- Self-starter mindset — comfortable working independently, with a bias toward
action.

- Passion for delivering outstanding customer experiences.

Why join us? 

- Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

- Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

- Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

- Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

- Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles 

Extreme Ownership 

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship 

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

title: Generalist (Workshops)
description:
Deliver workshops that help exceptional people pursue high-impact work in AI safety, biosecurity, and policy. 

Depending on experience, we consider candidates for the Generalist (Workshops) or Senior Generalist (Workshops) version of this role.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

- SPAR : The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

- Generator Residency : In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

- Global Challenges Project : A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

- Pathfinder Fellowship : Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

The Role

The Global Challenges Project (GCP) runs three-day residential workshops that help talented individuals explore careers in AI safety and biosecurity. Over the past few years, GCP has run dozens of workshops for 400+ students, mostly in Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. GCP has a long and successful track record and became part of Kairos in early 2026.

We’re now expanding GCP into a full portfolio of workshops serving different audiences and career stages, with the ambition of becoming the leading fieldbuilding workshop organizer in AI safety and biosecurity. This means building new programs, new formats, and the systems to deliver reliably at scale.

We’re looking for a generalist to help deliver our workshops. You’ll own the operational backbone of our events, including outreach, venues, travel, admissions logistics, guest coordination, inventory, and the systems that hold it all together. You’ll also attend some of our workshops and help run them in person.

This job requires agency as you’ll own the delivery of many key aspects of our workshops. You’ll need to spot problems before they happen, and improve our strategy and systems after every event. This role offers excellent opportunities for progression, and your scope and responsibility will grow with our portfolio.

What You’ll Do

- Own operational workstreams end to end. For each workshop, you’ll take responsibility for workstreams such as outreach, venue search and contracting, catering and dietary needs, participant and guest travel, inventory and materials, and on-site logistics.

- Run admissions and participant operations. You’ll build application and RSVP forms, help coordinate selection processes, send decisions, run onboarding communications, and make sure every participant arrives informed and prepared.

- Coordinate guests. High-quality guests are central to our workshops’ impact. You’ll track invitations, chase confirmations, and act as a point of contact so guests have a smooth experience from first email to follow-up.

- Deliver workshops in person. You’ll travel to some of our workshops (predominantly in the UK and US) and help run them on the ground.

- Build systems that scale. We run our events on Notion, Airtable, Linear, and a growing set of automations and custom code. You’ll help design and improve these systems and turn what we learn at each event into better playbooks and templates.

- Help shape our workshops strategy. You’ll work across GCP, OASIS, and our new workshop programs, and everyone on the team has a say in how Kairos’s events develop.

- Contribute to Kairos more broadly. As capacity allows, you’ll pitch in on our other programs like SPAR and Pathfinder, build relationships across the AI safety ecosystem, and ship small cross-team projects.

Who You Are

- An operations generalist with events experience. You’ve delivered events such as workshops, conferences, or retreats, or you’ve done demanding operational work and can show you’d thrive doing it for in-person events.

- Highly organized. You’ll juggle multiple workstreams across several workshops at once, each with its own deadlines. You have strong systems for keeping everything on track, and details don’t slip past you.

- High agency. You spot problems early and fix them without waiting to be asked, and you adapt when plans change on the day.

- A high quality bar. You check your own work before handing it over, and you care about getting the small things right because they’re important to the attendees’ experience.

- Good with people, and energized by workshops. Attending three-day residential events is part of this role. You’ll need the energy to engage warmly with participants and guests while keeping the event running smoothly.

- Mission-aligned. You care deeply about how the development of advanced AI and biotechnology plays out, and you believe workshops can be a highly effective way to help talented people enter these fields. Familiarity with the AI safety ecosystem is a plus, but not required.

Why Work With Us

- You’ll work toward reducing risks from advanced AI and biotechnology, two of the most important challenges of our time. Both fields need far more talented people than they have, and our workshops move promising people into careers working on them. The quality of our delivery is a big part of that impact.

- You’ll own your workstreams end to end, and you’ll see the results firsthand at every workshop.

- You’ll build on GCP’s strong brand, excellent reputation, and long track record, and help us grow into the leading workshop organizer in the space.

- You’ll work closely with high-profile guests across AI safety and biorisk, and develop a strong professional network.

- We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

What We Offer

- AI & Automation: Du identifizierst Automatisierungspotenziale in internen Prozessen und Geschäftsmodellen, testest KI-Tools und -Workflows und trägst aktiv dazu bei, wie Galvany künstliche Intelligenz operativ einsetzt – zur Effizienzsteigerung, Produktentwicklung und Entscheidungsfindung.

Benefits

title: General Manager (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand
description:
Managing Director (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand 

Location: Köln

Start: Ab sofort

Setup: Vollzeit (on-site)

THE BRAND & THE OPPORTUNITY 

Du baust gemeinsam mit uns eine neue Fitness-Marke im Segment Mid Cost - High Value auf.

Die Vision: „ Der neue Hotspot in der City für Workout, Recovery, Co-Working und Socializing.“ 

Kraft, Cardio und Functional, Live-Kurse, Sauna und Recovery, Bar und Lounge sowie eine ruhige Co-Working Zone, alles unter einem Dach - zu einem erschwinglichen Preis deutlich unter Premium-Clubs.

Unsere Clubs sollen auf ehemaligen Retail-Flächen entstehen, in 1A-Innenstadtlagen mit langfristig gesicherten Mietverträgen. Wir starten in Westdeutschland in der Region Köln, Essen, Frankfurt und expandieren dann.

Wir arbeiten mit unternehmerischem Anspruch: kleines Team, kurze Wege, jeder Standort muss sich selbst tragen. Der erste Club ist der Beweis für das Konzept, und jeder weitere wird durch den Erfolg des vorherigen verdient.

Für dich heißt das: Du bist ab Sekunde 1 dabei und gestaltest vom Namen über das Konzept bis hin zur Location alles von Grund auf mit. Kein Einstieg in einen bestehenden Betrieb, sondern die Chance, eine Marke von Null an aufzubauen , das Modell in allen Details zu gestalten und volle Verantwortung für das Ergebnis zu übernehmen.

THE ROLE & YOUR ROADMAP 

Als Managing Director verantwortest du den kompletten Aufbau der Marke - von den ersten Entwürfen auf dem Reißbrett bis hin zur Multi-Site-Skalierung.

- Phase 1 - Konzept schärfen: Du bringst das Angebot, das Flächenprogramm, die Pricing-Strategie und den Brand-Auftritt gemeinsam mit den Gesellschaftern zur Marktreife.

- Phase 2 - Ersten Club eröffnen: Du steuerst den Ausbau vor Ort, baust dein Kernteam auf, drehst den Pre-Opening-Sales auf Anschlag und bringst den ersten Flagship-Standort ans Netz.

- Phase 3 - Proof of Concept: Du erreichst mit dem Club die geplanten Mitglieder- und Ergebniszahlen (P&L) und machst aus dem Piloten ein hocheffizientes, wiederholbares Modell.

- Phase 4 - Skalieren: Du eröffnest weitere Standorte in Deutschland und baust die Organisation auf, die dieses Wachstum trägt.

YOUR IMPACT (DIE ERSTEN 12 MONATE) 

Du bist von Tag 1 an am Start und bringst den ersten Standort ans Netz:

- Konzept zur Marktreife bringen: Zusammen mit der Projektleitung feilst du an Angebot, Flächenaufteilung, Preisen und Marke.

- Ausbau steuern: Du betreust den Aus- und Umbau des ersten Standorts und behältst Zeit- und Kostenrahmen fest im Griff.

- Kernteam aufbauen: Du rekrutierst Club-Leitung, Trainer sowie Servicepersonal und prägst von Anfang an Kultur und Standards.

- Pre-Sales & Markteintritt verantworten: Du treibst die Mitgliedergewinnung vor der Eröffnung, machst lokales Marketing und schließt Deals mit Firmenkunden sowie Aggregatoren (z. B. Urban Sports Club, EGYM Wellpass).

- Prozesse & Tech aufsetzen: Du richtest Mitgliederverwaltung, Zugangssysteme, App und Reporting ein.

- Ersten Club eröffnen: Du begleitest das Grand Opening und führst den Standort erfolgreich in den Live-Betrieb.

YOUR PROFILE 

Du brennst selbst für Fitness und Lifestyle, denkst wie ein Unternehmer und hast den Biss, etwas Eigenes aufzubauen? Dann bist du genau die richtige Person!

- Track Record: Du hast Führungserfahrung in der Fitnessbranche (z. B. als Area Manager, Cluster Manager oder Regional Director), idealerweise mit P&L Verantwortung.

- Neueröffnungs-Erfahrung: Du hast schon eine Neueröffnung von A bis Z selbst verantwortet oder mitgestaltet (Ausbau, Teamaufbau, Pre-Sales).

- Business Mindset: Du hast Kaufmännisches Denken, Data-Drive und souveränes Auftreten gegenüber Gesellschaftern, Vermietern und Partnern.

- Hands-on & Drive: Du packst überall mit an, bis du zufrieden bist. Danach führst du ein wachsendes Team.

- Setup: Vollzeit, Wohnsitz oder Relocation in die Startregion Köln, Essen oder Frankfurt. Reisebereitschaft zu den Standorten und Deutsch C2.

Das wäre ein Plus: Vorerfahrung aus Hospitality, Wellness oder Gastronomie, Erfahrung im Markenaufbau sowie ein starkes Netzwerk in der Fitnessbranche.

WHY US 

- Maximale Gestaltungsfreiheit: Die seltene Chance, eine komplett neue Marke von der ersten Skizze an zu ownen.

- High-Speed & Support: Kurze Entscheidungswege und direkter Austausch mit den Gesellschaftern. Du entscheidest alles mit!

- Executive Package: Attraktive Vergütung bestehend aus Fixgehalt, transparentem Bonus und einem Firmenwagen.

Contact: Alex Berwanger

Key Account Director 
Full-time (40 hours per week), Hybrid (Berlin, Germany)

About Us 
At The Global Talent Co., we provide opportunities to work with leading innovative technology companies worldwide, offering stable employment, competitive compensation, career growth, and access to a community of 25,000+ like-minded marketing professionals.

About the Company 
You’ll be joining a Berlin-headquartered, founder-led company that has spent over a decade becoming one of Europe’s leading partners for premium custom signage, trusted by well-known brands in retail, luxury, automotive, hospitality and tech. - Structured and CRM-disciplined; pipeline management comes naturally

- Listens first and understands what matters to a client before pitching

Nice to Have

- Hands-on experience with tenders, RFPs and framework agreements

- An existing network among brand, retail marketing or visual merchandising leaders in DACH

title: Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d)
description:
The product you will work on The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. 

Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform. 

The ideal candidate is We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production. 

This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field. 

Your role and responsibilities You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams. 

Build the platform 

- Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters. 

- Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions. 

- Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment. 

- Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations. 

- Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services. 

- Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior 

- . 

Run what you build 

- Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code. 

- Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations. 

- Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code. 

- Be part of a compensated on-call rotation 

Set the technical direction 

- Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind. 

- Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate. 

- Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes. 

What you need to succeed in this role - Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems. 

- Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on. 

- Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy. 

- Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today. 

- Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack. 

- Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation. 

- A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change. 

- A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation. 

- Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems. 

- Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone. 

- Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists. 

- Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it. 

- A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone. 

- Experience in using AI for engineering. 

Nice to haves - Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production. 

- Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations. 

- Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it. 

- Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security. 

- Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6. 

- Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry. 

- Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects 

We offer you At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme. 

You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership. You’ll work on cutting-edge audio technology, turn complex requirements into working solutions and contribute to global projects, with support for your growth through individual development plans, mentoring and coaching.

title: Senior Director Software Engineering (f/m/d)
description:
Who we are and what you’ll do HOLOPLOT is seeking a decisive, technically strong and business-oriented Senior Director Software Engineering (f/m/d), to lead our 20-person software engineering organization, drive cross-functional delivery, and own the long-term software architecture for our high-performance audio products. 

Working closely with engineering leads who focus on deep technical problem-solving and team mentorship, this role leads overall software delivery, strategic technical vision, and cross-departmental alignment. 

Main objectives of the role As Senior Director Software Engineering (f/m/d), you will take full technical ownership of the end-to-end delivery of HOLOPLOT’s software ecosystem, spanning embedded and distributed Linux systems, audio DSP, 3D/GPU, C++, Rust and web-based front-end applications, Kubernetes cluster and cloud infrastructure. You will act as the operational bridge between software engineering, hardware development, research, product, customer success teams, and key enterprise clients. You will work closely with the Director of Product for Software as well as the CPO, and report to the CTO. 

Your role and responsibilities - Strategic Software Vision & Architecture : Own and drive the strategic vision for the technical backbone of the HOLOPLOT product ecosystem. Proactively identify architectural risks and ensure performance and scalability across embedded hardware, audio processing platforms, and user interfaces. 

- Execution & High-Stakes Delivery : Take full accountability for software delivery timeliness, quality, and reliability. Proactively lead critical client-facing missions, OS rollouts, and on-site integration handovers (e.g., venue acceptance testing and integration protocols), including regular international travel 

- High-Performing Mission-Driven Teams : Attract, grow, and retain strong engineering talent to build highly successful, cross-functional product development teams. Foster a culture of excellence, ownership, agency, and innovation that drives high employee engagement, productivity, and strong outcomes for our customers. 

- Cross-Functional Alignment : Drive seamless collaboration between Software, Research, Customer Success, Product Management, and external technical partners (such as client IT security and external system integrators). Eliminate inter-departmental friction and establish clear integration pathways. 

- Business-First Leadership : Together with Product, align software priorities and architecture directly with HOLOPLOT’s strategic and commercial objectives. Make decisive, well-reasoned trade-offs under pressure while optimizing engineering output for maximum company value. 

- Operational Leadership & Partnering : Partner with dedicated Engineering Managers and Tech Leads who oversee team culture, individual mentoring, and deeply technical topics. Foster a culture of engineering excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Focus your impact on operational discipline, accountability, and clear departmental direction. 

- AI Strategy & Development Workflows : Define and execute HOLOPLOT's AI strategy for software development. Integrate AI-assisted engineering tools, automated workflows, and emerging AI technologies into the software development life cycle to elevate team productivity and explore modern product capabilities. 

- Platform, Quality & Operational Excellence: Ensure high standards of quality, reliability, maintainability, and scalability across all software solutions. Identify, assess, and mitigate technological risks, including technical debt and platform lifecycle challenges. Define and improve engineering processes, development standards, and tooling to enable predictable, high-quality delivery. 

- Security, Compliance & Risk Management: Drive HOLOPLOT’s technology security strategy, including cybersecurity, data protection, and secure-by-design principles. Ensure compliance with relevant industry standards, validation/certifications, and regulatory requirements. Ensure systems are resilient, reliable, and fit for production and customer use. 

What you need to succeed in this role - Engineering Leadership : Extensive experience managing software teams of significant size (15-30+ engineers) in complex, multi-disciplinary technology environments 

- Deep-Tech Literacy : Comfortable navigating a highly heterogeneous tech stack encompassing Low-Level/Embedded C++ & Rust, Audio DSP, 3D/GPU rendering, Linux, Kubernetes, NATS, gRPC, JUCE, CI/CD and Web services. 

- Track Record of Ownership : Proven experience driving complex hardware-software product rollouts and managing high-stakes client or partner integrations end-to-end. 

- Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management : Strong diplomacy and technical communication skills, with a track record of bridging engineering teams with business, product, research, and client stakeholders. 

- Pragmatic Decision-Making : Ability to operate with high clarity and a steady hand in fast-paced environments, prioritizing long-term product stability over short-term friction. 

- AI-Driven Development Strategy : Demonstrated experience establishing AI-development strategies and driving the practical adoption of AI-assisted software development, LLM tooling, or automated engineering workflows. 

- Audio Software and Hardware Products: Experience with the Pro Audio and Music Technology product space, as both developer and user. 

We offer you At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. We offer a competitive compensation package aligned with the scope and impact of this leadership role, along with perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme. 

You'll join an international, open-minded team and work directly with our C-level, engineering and product leads, as well as cross-functional stakeholders in customer success, research, and operations. You'll shape the strategic direction of our software architecture, own high-stakes delivery for cutting-edge audio technology, and drive the AI-assisted development strategy for a 20-person software engineering team, with the autonomy and accountability that comes with a senior leadership mandate.

title: AI Trainers Network - Arabic
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Trainers Network – Arabic based in Germany. 

Join a global network of language professionals and culturally aware contributors helping shape the future of artificial intelligence.
In this flexible, remote opportunity, you can contribute to projects that improve the accuracy, relevance, and inclusivity of AI systems.
Depending on your skills and availability, you may work on text, image, or audio annotation, content evaluation, and prompt creation.
Your Arabic language expertise and cultural understanding will help make AI-generated content more natural, reliable, and representative of diverse communities.
Projects vary in scope and duration, offering opportunities to gain experience with emerging AI technologies while working on your own terms.
This is a talent network opportunity rather than an active job opening, meaning you will be contacted when a suitable project becomes available.
Before each project begins, you will receive clear information about the tasks, timeline, and compensation so you can decide whether it fits your interests and availability.

Accountabilities 

As a contributor to the AI Trainers Network, you will support projects designed to improve AI performance, language understanding, and content quality. Depending on the project requirements and your areas of expertise, your responsibilities may include:

- 
Annotating and labeling text, images, or audio to help train and improve AI models.

- 
Evaluating search results, advertisements, and chatbot responses for accuracy, relevance, quality, and usefulness.

- 
Creating, testing, and refining prompts to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs).

- 
Reviewing AI-generated content to ensure linguistic accuracy, natural Arabic expression, and cultural appropriateness.

- 
Identifying errors, inconsistencies, and potentially misleading or unsuitable content in AI outputs.

- 
Applying project-specific guidelines and quality standards while maintaining consistency and attention to detail.

- 
Contributing feedback that helps develop safer, more inclusive, and human-centered AI systems.

- 
Managing assigned tasks independently and meeting project deadlines according to agreed requirements and availability.

Requirements

We are looking for detail-oriented, curious, and adaptable contributors who are interested in language, technology, and the development of AI systems. The ideal candidate combines strong Arabic language skills with the ability to evaluate information critically and work independently in a digital environment.

- 
Native or near-native fluency in Arabic, with a strong understanding of grammar, vocabulary, and linguistic nuances.

- 
Current residence in Poland for this opportunity.

- 
Good English proficiency to understand project instructions and communicate effectively.

- 
Comfort using digital tools, online platforms, and web-based applications.

- 
Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify linguistic, factual, and contextual inconsistencies.

- 
Good analytical and critical-thinking skills, particularly when evaluating content for accuracy and relevance.

- 
Cultural awareness and an understanding of Arabic-speaking communities, communication styles, and regional language variations.

- 
Ability to follow detailed guidelines, work independently, and deliver consistent, high-quality results.

- 
Curiosity about artificial intelligence, language technologies, and how human feedback can improve AI systems.

- 
Flexibility to participate in projects of varying durations and complexity, depending on your availability.

Previous experience in data annotation, content evaluation, translation, linguistics, prompt engineering, or AI training may be helpful, but project-specific requirements will vary.

Benefits

- 
Flexible, remote work: Contribute to suitable projects from your preferred working environment, subject to individual project requirements.

- 
Control over your availability: Choose whether to participate when a project matches your schedule and interests.

- 
Project-based opportunities: Access assignments that may last from a few days to several weeks, depending on scope and demand.

- 
Transparent compensation: Receive project-specific details about payment, tasks, and timelines before deciding whether to participate.

- 
Practical AI experience: Develop your understanding of AI training, data annotation, language evaluation, and large language models.

- 
Meaningful contribution: Help build more accurate, inclusive, and culturally aware AI technologies.

- 
Global contributor community: Become part of an international network of people contributing their linguistic and cultural expertise.

- 
Opportunities to grow: Build relevant skills through exposure to different projects and evolving AI technologies.

title: Account Executive
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Account Executive based in Germany. 

As an Account Executive, you will drive business growth across Europe by selling cutting-edge cloud infrastructure technology to enterprise customers, cloud providers, and fast-growing AI and developer platforms. You will own the entire sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery to technical evaluations, pilot programs, commercial negotiations, and closing deals. Working closely with the founding team and technical experts, you will help customers understand how next-generation microvirtualization can improve workload isolation, security, and infrastructure efficiency. You will build a qualified pipeline through strategic outbound campaigns, industry networking, and targeted account development. As an early sales hire, you will have a direct influence on the go-to-market strategy, sales processes, and future growth of the commercial organization. This fully remote opportunity combines entrepreneurial ownership, technical learning, and uncapped earning potential in a rapidly evolving AI and cloud infrastructure market.

Accountabilities 

- 
Build, manage, and grow a European sales pipeline targeting enterprise infrastructure teams, cloud and hosting providers, and high-growth AI and developer technology companies.

- 
Own the full sales cycle, from identifying and qualifying prospects to conducting discovery calls, coordinating technical evaluations, negotiating commercial terms, and securing signed contracts.

- 
Develop and execute targeted outbound strategies in collaboration with go-to-market engineers, identifying priority accounts, key decision-makers, and effective messaging to generate qualified opportunities.

- 
Lead customer conversations and engage economic buyers early, building relationships with CTOs, platform engineering leaders, security teams, procurement professionals, and other stakeholders involved in complex purchasing decisions.

- 
Coordinate product demonstrations, technical deep dives, and proof-of-concept or pilot programs alongside founders and field engineers to demonstrate product value and accelerate customer adoption.

- 
Translate technical capabilities into clear business outcomes, showing customers how lightweight microvirtual machines can improve workload isolation, infrastructure utilization, security, and deployment speed.

- 
Apply structured qualification methodologies, including MEDDPICC, to assess deal quality, understand decision-making processes, identify risks, and convert successful pilots into long-term production commitments.

- 
Develop commercial proposals tailored to customer requirements, including usage-based pricing, minimum commitments, dedicated deployments, and bring-your-own-cloud arrangements.

- 
Identify opportunities for account expansion by working closely with field engineers and existing customers to understand evolving infrastructure needs and increase adoption.

- 
Represent the business at industry conferences, cloud-native events, AI infrastructure gatherings, and regional meetups, building relationships and converting networking opportunities into qualified pipeline.

-

Wir setzen uns für ein diverses und inklusives Umfeld ein. Gemeinsam als ein Team aus über 50 Nationen mit unseren verschiedenen Fähigkeiten, Ideen und Erfahrungen arbeiten wir aktiv daran, Vielfalt im Unternehmen zu repräsentieren.

description:
Who We Are 

At Partnerize, we're on a mission to transform the way businesses grow. We've built the leading partnership automation platform that empowers brands to discover, engage, and convert their audiences at scale. From affiliate marketing to influencer collaborations, we help our clients build and manage profitable partnerships that drive real results. We're a team of passionate problem-solvers who are dedicated to helping our clients win in the ever-evolving world of digital marketing.

Why Join Us 

We're looking for passionate, talented people who want to be part of a winning team. At Partnerize, you'll find a culture of collaboration, innovation, and respect. We're guided by our core values, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. We also offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, and a flexible work environment that allows you to thrive both personally and professionally. If you're ready to grow your career and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

This role operates on a hybrid basis and requires attendance in our Newcastle office once a week. While some flexibility may be discussed, applicants should be willing and able to work from the office as part of the role. 

The Role 

We are looking for a Senior Infrastructure Manager who is, first and foremost, a people leader.

In this role, your primary responsibility is the health, performance, and career growth of your engineering team. While you must possess a solid technical background to understand the challenges your team faces, your day-to-day focus will not be hands-on technical work. Instead, you will use your experience to remove blockers, guide decision-making, and ensure your engineers have the environment they need to succeed.

The Team You Will Lead 

You will lead the Infrastructure Solutions team within the wider Technical Operations department. Your engineers are responsible for building the environment, delivering projects as requested by Engineering and Product, and ensuring we remain available, scalable, and secure. They are not responsible for the BAU function of the platforms that is managed by another team within Technical Operations. The Infrastructure Solutions team takes a concept or idea and makes that into a reality within the boundaries and constraints of our platforms. 

You will be managing a team of engineers who individually possess experience in:

- On-Premise Linux systems, Container solutions, Debian packaging, Ansible, data streaming and queuing technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ

- Advanced database management knowledge (MySQL, Postgres) in replicated environments.

- Physical Network management, with an on-prem estate that is Juniper focused. 

- Cloud environments: GCP and AWS

- Platform engineer focused on building, maintaining and supporting an Internal Developer Platform (CI/CD)

The Operational Reality 

It is important to be transparent about the environment you are joining. We operate at high velocity with a broad and complex technology estate. However, we are a lean team, not a giant corporation with endless resources.

- Context Switching is the Norm

- You will rarely have the luxury of focusing on a single task for weeks at a time. You will be required to shift focus multiple times a week, and sometimes multiple times a day, as business priorities evolve.

- Agility over Silos

- Because we are a lean team, we wear many hats. You must be comfortable pivoting from a strategic discussion to an operational challenge without losing momentum.

- Focus Management

- Success in this role requires the ability to maintain high standards while navigating a workload that changes dynamically. This is not a role for those who prefer a slow, singular focus; it is for those who thrive on variety, pace, and solving complex problems in real-time.

As the Senior Infrastructure Manager, You Will: 

People Leadership & Talent Development 

- Team Management

- Lead, mentor, and motivate a team of infrastructure engineers. Conduct weekly 1-2-1s, manage performance reviews, and handle all aspects of people management.

- Formal Training & Growth

- Go beyond ad-hoc mentoring to schedule and lead formal training sessions regarding operational improvements. Actively create professional development plans for your direct reports.

- Recruitment & Retention

- Own the hiring process for your team, ensuring we attract top talent and maintain a supportive, inclusive culture.

- Culture of Learning

- Foster a "Self-Learner" mindset. Create a transparent environment where failures are treated as learning opportunities and documented as such for future reference.

Strategic & Operational Management 

- Budget & Capacity Planning

- Ability to own your team's budget and lead capacity planning initiatives. You will forecast future infrastructure needs to ensure we remain scalable while managing spend for subscriptions and hardware.

- Risk & Contingency

- Proactively identify operational risks and form contingency plans immediately to ensure business continuity.

- Procedure & Frameworks

- Ability to define, maintain, and cascade operational procedures (SOPs) and ITIL standards.

- Prioritisation

- Shield your team from noise by effectively prioritising workloads (Changes, Problems, and Projects) and managing stakeholder expectations.

Technical Support & Oversight 

- Performance Optimisation

- Measure and optimise system performance with a focus on improving reliability and time-to-market. You will drive innovation to get ahead of internal customer needs rather than just reacting to them.

- Visual Documentation

- Ensure the team produces detailed system design documentation, specifically enforcing the inclusion of visual representations to support understanding. Ability to technologically assess it as a technical editor.

- Hybrid Estate Management

- Ability to oversee the management of both On-Premise and Cloud (GCP/AWS), ensuring high availability across all environments.

- Unblocking Issues

- Act as the senior escalation point for complex technical issues. Your goal is not to fix the issue yourself, but to coordinate the right resources and provide air cover.

General Duties 

On-Call Duties Willingness to participate in the Management On-Call Rotation to support the department and the business (Current frequency: Once every three weeks). Ad-Hoc Carry out other strategic or technical duties required to support the Director/VP of Technical Operations. 

Essential Knowledge, Skills, and Experience 

Leadership & Management Competencies 

- Proven Management Experience

- Significant experience leading a technical team, with a specific focus on the people management aspect (performance reviews, career growth etc).

- Project Management

- Strong project management experience with the ability to delegate effectively to meet tight deadlines. You must be able to multitask and maintain focus in a high-priority environment.

- Communication

- Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. You must be able to liaise effectively with management and other business areas. Engagement may also include interactions with senior technical engineers/leaders within other teams and C-Team members. 

- Goal Oriented

A fully owned and operated ecosystem that converges the two worlds of sports media and sports betting. We're proud of the high ratings for our commitment to excellence and fueling fan's passion for sport driving us to the top.

Every day, our team embody our values: adaptability, teamwork, a fan-driven approach, and an ever-curious mindset that fuels our ambition. Key Responsibilities 

- Technical Leadership and Guidance:  Act as a primary technical point of contact and subject matter expert for specific data engineering projects or domains, guiding team members through complex technical challenges and promoting innovative solutions.

- End-to-End Data Solution Development:  Design, develop, test, and deploy highly scalable, reliable, and fault-tolerant data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes. This includes data ingestion from diverse sources, data transformation, and data loading into various data stores (e.g., data warehouses, data lakes).

- Architectural Implementation:  Work closely with Data Architects to translate architectural blueprints and standards into concrete implementations, ensuring new data components align with the overall data strategy and infrastructure requirements.

- Mentorship and Skill Development:  Actively mentor and coach junior and mid-level data engineers, providing constructive feedback, sharing technical knowledge, and fostering their growth in coding, data modeling, and general data engineering best practices.

- Hands-On Contribution:  Maintain a significant hands-on role in coding, data modeling, infrastructure-as-code development, and platform configuration, leading by example and ensuring high-quality output.

- Data Quality and Performance Assurance:  Take direct responsibility for ensuring the quality, integrity, and performance of data assets within their assigned domain or projects, implementing monitoring, validation, and optimization strategies.

- Operational Efficiency and Cost Optimization:  Proactively identify and implement technical optimizations for data processing, storage, and infrastructure utilization to improve efficiency, reduce operational costs, and enhance system performance.

- Code Review and Best Practices:  Lead and participate in rigorous code reviews, advocating for and enforcing engineering best practices, coding standards, and architectural patterns to maintain high code quality and system stability.

- Complex Problem Solving:  Diagnose, troubleshoot, and provide effective solutions for highly complex data-related issues, incidents, and performance bottlenecks, often working under pressure.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration:  Collaborate effectively with other engineering teams, product managers, data scientists, and business stakeholders to understand data requirements, integrate solutions, and provide technical insights.

Skills, Knowledge and Experience 

- Advanced Data Pipeline Expertise:  Proven, in-depth experience as a senior or lead data engineer with a strong portfolio of hands-on contributions to designing, building, and optimizing complex, large-scale data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes.

- Enterprise Data Warehousing (EDW) and Data Modeling:  Strong practical experience with EDW concepts, principles, and implementation, specifically including the design and practical application of a single, integrated data model for analytical purposes.

- Cloud Data Platforms:  Hands-on experience with cloud-native data services and infrastructure on at least one major cloud provider (e.g., AWS services like S3, Redshift, Glue, EMR; GCP services like BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub; Azure services like Data Lake, Synapse Analytics).

- Cost Optimization Strategies:  Demonstrated ability to identify, propose, and implement technical solutions that lead to significant cost savings in data processing, storage, and infrastructure within a large-scale data environment.

- Software Engineering Fundamentals:  Expert proficiency in software development methodologies (e.g., Agile, Scrum), version control (Git), CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and comprehensive understanding of software engineering best practices.

- Programming Languages:  Exceptional coding skills in at least one relevant programming language (e.g., Python, Scala, Java, JavaScript, C/C++), with a focus on writing clean, efficient, and maintainable code.

- Database Systems:  Extensive experience with various database technologies including relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL), NoSQL databases (e.g., MongoDB, Cassandra), and analytical data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery).

- Data Architecture Principles:  Solid understanding of data architecture patterns (e.g., Data Mesh, Data Lakehouse, Lambda/Kappa architectures), distributed systems, and their practical application.

- Regulatory Reporting:  Practical experience in developing and maintaining robust and auditable data solutions for regulatory reporting, particularly within the gaming or other highly regulated industries.

- AI: Fluent in AI prompting alongside staying ahead of emerging AI technologies.

- Technical Leadership & Mentorship:  A natural leader who can effectively guide, inspire, and technically mentor junior and mid-level engineers. Possesses the ability to break down complex problems, provide clear direction, and foster a learning environment, thereby enhancing team capabilities and promoting adherence to best practices.

title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Senior Infrastructure Engineer 

Remote (UK-based), with occasional on-site work at our data centres | Full-Time

About Us 

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year ( Risk.net ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world’s leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what’s technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role 

We’re looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to help run and grow the network and cloud estate behind our trading platform. Networking in our colocation data centres is the core of the role. The estate spans London, New York and Singapore, and from Q1 2027 a new Tokyo data centre.

This is a hands-on role in a small, expert infrastructure team. You’ll work closely with our Head of Infrastructure, following problems from the cross-connect through hosts, containers and AWS. You’ll also help keep infrastructure delivery on track, from timelines and reporting to working closely with our TechOps team.

What You’ll Work On 

- Low-latency networking across our colocation sites: switching and routing, cross-connects, BGP peering with liquidity providers and clients, and the fabric that carries our trading traffic

- Bringing new sites to application-ready, starting with Tokyo

- Our hybrid connectivity into multi-region AWS, including Direct Connect, routing and failover

- Linux hosts and containers on the critical path, with every change made through code (Ansible, Git, Terraform), never by hand

- Monitoring and alerting that catches problems before clients do, plus runbooks and post-incident reviews that someone else can follow

- Planning and capacity: forecasting growth, setting timelines and reporting progress to TechOps and engineering

What We Need 

- 4+ years running production infrastructure in a latency-sensitive environment, such as HFT, an exchange, market data or bank trading infrastructure

- Strong networking: hands-on routing and switching (MLAG, LACP, VLANs), BGP in production, and a solid grasp of low-latency behaviour such as buffers, microbursts and congestion handling

- Colocation experience: cabinets, cross-connects, remote hands and vendor management

- Solid Linux (RHEL) and TCP/IP, and the ability to trace a problem from the wire to the application

- Infrastructure as code and containers as your default way of working

- Working knowledge of AWS networking, and the confidence to pick up the rest of our stack. Networking depth matters more to us than any particular cloud or platform tooling

- Methodical, evidence-led troubleshooting and clear documentation

A strong plus: 

- Project management experience: owning timelines, reporting progress, and working with ops teams to hit deadlines

- Kernel bypass (Onload/ef_vi), PTP and time synchronisation

- Experience bringing up a new colo site

- FIX protocol or OTC FX market knowledge

- Python for tooling

Working pattern: Infrastructure changes are often scheduled outside trading hours, including weekends, and the team shares an on-call rota. We’re a team with flexible hours, so time worked out of hours is taken back during the week. Day-to-day work is remote, with occasional visits to our data centres, most often in London (Slough).

What You Get 

- Real ownership of a live global trading network, hands-on, with few layers of process

- A build-out year, with a new Tokyo data centre in Q1 and more growth ahead

- A senior seat in a small, expert team where your changes ship and are measured

- Competitive package — up to 38 days leave (inc. bank holidays), private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

- Remote-friendly working with flexibility around out-of-hours work

- Growth as the estate scales

We believe in transparency, honest feedback and writing things down, and we aim to build systems that don’t depend on the heroics of individuals.

Our Hiring Process 

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages:

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Technical Deep Dive with our Head of Infrastructure
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~90 minutes

Stage 3: Leadership Conversation with our CDO
Format: Video call, ~45 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you’re invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

How to Apply 

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you’ll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we’re happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy.

QUALIFICATIONS

- Ability to establish as a trusted advisor for scientists, and successfully pitch to scientific buyers.

We need someone who can hit the ground running, operate independently and turn opportunities into results.

Build and activate strategic partnerships

- Convert existing interest into active, commercially productive partnerships while proactively opening new doors.

Turn partnerships into revenue 

- Drive partner opportunities from initial engagement through commercial negotiation, agreement and activation.

- Build joint account plans, identify customer opportunities and develop a qualified pipeline with clear commercial objectives.

- Work with partners and internal sales teams to progress opportunities into pilots, deployments and revenue.

- Take accountability for outcomes. Signed agreements matter, but active partners, customer engagements and revenue matter more.

Create propositions that partners can sell

Get hands-on and make things happen

- Navigate commercial, technical and organisational challenges to keep deals moving.

- Build the processes, reporting and partner engagement model needed to scale what works, without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

___________________________________________________________________________

What we’re looking for 

We want someone who has built partnerships that generate business, not simply managed relationships.

You'll bring:

- A proven commercial track record. Demonstrable success building partnerships, developing pipeline and delivering revenue within enterprise technology, software or AI.

- Strong SI and consultancy experience. You understand how these organisations operate, how to navigate their internal structures and what it takes to turn strategic alignment into real customer opportunities.

- Commercial sharpness. You know how to qualify opportunities, negotiate agreements, develop compelling commercial propositions and focus effort where it delivers the greatest return.

- Technical credibility. You're comfortable engaging with complex enterprise technology, running product demonstrations and holding meaningful conversations with technical stakeholders. You don't need to be an engineer, but you must be capable of getting under the skin of our products.

- Executive-level relationship skills. You can engage confidently with senior decision-makers, build credibility quickly and influence stakeholders across large organisations.

- Relentless execution. You're proactive, resourceful and commercially driven. You take ownership, follow through and don't need someone else to create momentum.

- An entrepreneurial mindset. You thrive in fast-moving environments, make sound decisions with incomplete information and are equally comfortable shaping strategy and doing the work yourself.

Experience working with government, defence, financial services or other regulated industries would be a strong advantage.

Above all, we're looking for someone with the ambition, judgement and drive to build something exceptional.

Work on technology that matters. Our sovereign LLM ambition and broader AI portfolio address some of the biggest challenges facing enterprises and governments today. You'll help build the partnerships that take these capabilities into the real world.

A genuine opportunity to make an impact. We're already seeing significant partner interest. You'll have the opportunity to convert that momentum into commercial results and play a direct role in our growth.

Ownership, not bureaucracy. You'll have meaningful responsibility, direct access to decision-makers and the freedom to shape how we build our partner ecosystem. We're moving quickly, and we value people who make things happen.

Build something from the ground up. This is an opportunity to help define Cosine's partnership strategy and establish relationships that could become fundamental to how we scale.

Come and build with us 

We're looking for someone who's ambitious, commercially driven and excited by the opportunity to help bring frontier AI technology to market.

Someone who can think strategically, roll their sleeves up and deliver.

description:
About Fractile 

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

The Role 

About the Software organisation at Fractile 

Developer Experience sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing.

About the team and role 

The Developer Experience team at Fractile helps shape how our customers interact with the Fractile inference accelerator. We work across the company to identify, create, and present information on how the system is being used, as well as providing the tooling to help optimise our customers' usage of the system, while keeping a shallow learning curve.

As a member of the Developer Experience team you will need to understand the current state of development for inference hardware. You will need to be able to identify what will work well for engineers wanting to identify potential opportunities for performance improvements, while knowing what tooling will fit into an existing LLM engineer's workflow with the minimal amount of disruption and effort.

About you 

We're looking for someone who is self-driven and capable of identifying tooling opportunities, designing those tools, and delivering them in a way which will fit in with an LLM engineer's existing toolset. You will have worked in this area before, possibly as an FDE or at a company that provides inference services using their own models, and have the ability to develop new tools that are designed to be functional and easy to learn and use.

Key Requirements 

- Experience with inference frameworks such as JAX and/or PyTorch

- Experience of software development in Python, Rust, C/C++, or a similar language

- Experience monitoring and optimising code written in CUDA, ROCm, OpenCL, or similar

- Experience monitoring and optimising LLM deployments with 50+ billion parameters

- Experience working with stakeholders across multiple teams

What We Offer 

- Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role

- Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation

- Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance

- Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment

title: Data Scientist - Broker Flow
description:
Data Scientist - Broker Flow Team

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the Broker Flow team. 

You'll own the experiments that shape the journey brokers use to apply on their clients' behalf. Brokers are one of iwoca's main routes to new customers.

The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team 

Broker Flow, a new team in iwoca's third-party acquisition department, owns the journey for businesses that come to iwoca through a broker – from before they apply to a completed credit assessment. Its aim is to get more of those businesses to an offer. Broker Terms, a separate team, then sets the price, amount, and duration of each offer.

The team works on three parts of that journey:

- Broker engagement. Working with brokers and their clients before an application starts.

- The application. Making it smooth to complete, and collecting the data a credit decision needs.

- Operations. Running the CRM tools iwoca's teams work in, and automating operational processes.

The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use.

The role 

As the Data Scientist in Broker Flow, you'll give the team the evidence behind its product decisions. The core of the work is experiment design and causal inference, with modelling and analysis alongside it.

You'll own each project end to end. You'll frame the problem, choose the method, build the model or run the test, and take the answer to the commercial and strategy colleagues who act on it. You'll also meet brokers in person, which gives you the context to ask the right questions. The team is new, so its methods are yours to shape. You'll see the effect of your work in how many businesses reach an offer, and in their lifetime value.

You'll work with data scientists in iwoca's other broker and partner teams, and join the analytics guild – iwoca's data science community – to compare methods and build your expertise. Your results reach the wider business through Learnings, short write-ups that iwoca shares at weekly and fortnightly sessions.

Live project examples:

- Refinancing. Modelling which businesses would benefit from refinancing their existing borrowing, and testing a product for them.

- Stalled applications. Finding where broker applications stall, and testing fixes – from clearer emails and portal updates to an early offer that encourages document upload.

- Reintroductions. Testing the best moment for brokers to bring existing iwoca customers back to borrow.

- Approval probability. Measuring how well the estimate brokers see in the Introducer Portal predicts actual credit decisions, and making it more accurate.

- Measuring impact. Designing early signals – at sign-up and once documents are in – that predict a business's lifetime value, so the team can judge its changes quickly.

The requirements 

Essential:

- Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work.

- Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead.

- Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it.

- Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries.

- AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – an analysis pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't, and you check its output before anyone acts on it.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in commercial and strategy roles.

Bonus:

- Modelling depth. You've built or adapted statistical or ML models and can explain the maths behind them.

- Stochastic methods. You've used stochastic processes for inference or time-series modelling.

- Broker market insight. You've worked with brokers or other intermediaries in lending or financial services.

- Coding. You can write code for analysis. The team works in Python.

The salary 

We expect to pay from £70,000 to £100,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture 

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices 

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits 

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

title: Solutions Architect - EMEA
description:
About Us 

AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and exploited, then delivers fixes that won’t break the application. Security teams get evidence instead of noise, and developers get fixes instead of tickets.

The companies building AI trust us to secure it - our customers include OpenAI, SpaceX, DoorDash, Dropbox, Atlassian, MongoDB, Snowflake, Robinhood and Peloton to name a few.
