title: AI Support Engineer Lead
description:
About Dust 

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. 

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. 

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 .

Summary 

At Dust, we're building for a new kind of AI Operator : people who rethink and rebuild how their teams work around AI. Not “how can AI help us do this faster?” but “if AI existed from day one, would we even do this the same way?” 

As our AI Support Engineering Lead , you'll own how Support is built and scaled at Dust. This is a deeply hands-on role. You'll take on the hardest customer issues when our agents fall short, but your job isn't simply to resolve them. You'll look for the pattern behind each issue and turn what you learn into better agents, automation, tooling, documentation, and product improvements. Over time, you'll help grow the team and shape how Support Engineering operates as Dust scales.

You'll define, ship, and continuously iterate on the systems that make this possible: AI agents, automation workflows, classification systems, knowledge systems, and tooling built on top of Dust itself. You'll dogfood the product harder than almost anyone at the company and set the standard for how the rest of the Support Engineering team does the same.

We're looking for someone who wants to lead from the work: technically strong, obsessed with building better systems, and excited to shape both the team and the function as we grow. 

What you'll do 

Build the AI systems that do the work

- Set the technical direction for the support stack: what gets automated, in what order, and to what standard. You make the calls, not just the builds.

- Design, ship, and maintain AI agents and automation workflows that reduce manual support load: think ticket classification, acknowledgment automation, response drafting, incident detection, and proactive user outreach.

- Identify recurring categories of issues and engineer them out of existence through automation, documentation, prompt iteration, or product feedback.

- Build and maintain tooling (MCP integrations, Dust agents, internal scripts) that increase the team's capacity without increasing headcount.

- Define and own the "Support as a Product" backlog. You decide what goes on it, coach the team to execute it, and hold the bar on what shipped means.

Run support when the systems fall short

- Hire, onboard, and develop the support engineers around you. You're not just resolving tickets and building systems, you're growing the people who will.

- Set the standard for how complex issues get handled at Dust. You take the hardest tickets yourself. The team knows what good looks like because they've watched you do it.

- Investigate complex issues across logs, code, and internal tooling to identify root causes and provide clear answers to customers.

- Handle escalated cases with precise, accessible communication for both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Systematically analyze agent-generated responses for inconsistencies and iterate on prompts, documentation, and tooling until human intervention is minimal.

Bridge customer pain to product improvements

- Represent support at the engineering and product level. You synthesize signal, prioritize it, and push it through with enough context that it actually moves things, not just relays it.

- Build strong working relationships with engineers and customer-facing teams to ensure efficient, high-context escalations.

- Own the feedback loop end-to-end: when agents fail due to missing or incorrect information, close the gap across engineering, product, and documentation.

Requirements 

Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions: Aptitude, Attitude and Agency.

Aptitude

- Function-building experience: You've defined or significantly shaped a support engineering function before: built the operating model, set the standards, hired into the team, or rebuilt a broken process from scratch.

- High technical aptitude: comfortable reading code, analyzing logs, navigating codebases, and troubleshooting distributed systems. You're not stopped by a stack trace.

- AI fluency at builder level: track record of building custom agents, automations, or workflows using AI tools (Dust, Cursor, Claude Code, n8n, etc.); not just prompting.

- Exceptional prioritization: You know what to solve immediately, what to automate, what to escalate, and, critically, what to delegate and to whom. You make these calls for yourself and for the team, fast and without second-guessing.

- People leadership: You've coached and developed engineers and know how to set expectations, give direct feedback, and raise the performance of the people around you.

- Bidirectional communication: can translate technical concepts to non-technical audiences and speak technical language fluently with engineers.

- Build/Run mindset: You believe the best Support Engineering teams don't just resolve issues. They build systems that prevent those issues from recurring.

Attitude

- Builder mentality: You instinctively automate repetitive work rather than accepting inefficient systems, and you hold your team to the same standard.

- Resilience-empathy paradox: You can absorb customer frustration without taking it personally while still deeply caring about the user experience.

- Leads by example: You're not above the queue. When something is hard, you take it.

- Exceptional prioritization: You know what to solve immediately, what to automate, and what to escalate.

- Thrives in ambiguity: You enjoy building systems from scratch in environments where many processes are still undefined.

- Low ego, team player: You share knowledge freely and care about the success of the broader team.

Agency

- High ownership: You define what needs to be done as often as you execute it. You don't wait for someone to tell you the function has a gap.

- Systems-first thinking: You focus on eliminating categories of work, not simply resolving tickets faster. You hold yourself and the team accountable to that distinction.

- Pattern recognition to repeatability: You turn recurring issues into scalable systems, automations, workflows, or documentation that eliminate future occurrences.

- Deep investigation instincts: You investigate as far as possible before escalating, providing engineering teams with thoughtful, high-context information when collaboration is needed, and you coach the team to do the same.

Even if you don’t meet every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. We care deeply about curiosity, potential, and determination, and we know exceptional people don’t always fit neatly into a checklist.

Benefits & Compensation 

- Competitive compensation based on level and experience

- 100,000€ - 160,000€

- Significant equity package at a Sequoia-backed startup

- Health benefits for you and your dependents

- New MacBook Pro or Linux machine, monitor, keyboard, etc.

- Opportunity to travel between our Paris and San Francisco offices

- Regular team events and off-sites

Location 

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust 

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. 

Learn how we think and work.

title: Head of ClinOps Data Management RWD/RWE
description:
À propos de Lifen

Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales peuvent transformer le système de santé, à condition qu’elles soient accessibles. Mieux les faire circuler, c’est réduire la charge administrative, mieux coordonner les soins et accélérer la recherche clinique.

Depuis 2015, nous développons des solutions qui aident les professionnels de santé à partager les informations médicales et les chercheurs à exploiter des données de santé. Plus de 150 personnes travaillent chez Lifen, depuis nos bureaux et à distance. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé en France.

Notre équipe

L’équipe Clinical Ops intervient au cœur de nos projets de recherche clinique fondés sur des données de santé. Elle transforme des documents médicaux en données structurées, nécessaires à la constitution de cohortes patients et à la préparation des exports utilisés dans nos projets de recherche.

Aujourd’hui, l’équipe structure environ 100 à 200 cas patients par semaine . Notre ambition : tripler cette capacité dans les 9 prochains mois, tout en maintenant un haut niveau de qualité des données.

Pour y parvenir, nous cherchons une personne capable de reprendre le management de l’équipe, mais surtout de piloter le flux de production, d’anticiper la charge et de porter une démarche d’amélioration continue avec les équipes Produit, IA et Engineering.

C’est un rôle à la croisée du management opérationnel, de la RWD et de l’amélioration de processus .

Ce que tu feras chez nous

Ta première mission sera de reprendre le pilotage de la production des cohortes afin d’en améliorer simultanément la qualité, la capacité de traitement et le niveau d’automatisation .

Concrètement, tu seras amené·e à :

- Manager et faire grandir l’équipe Clinical Ops, en donnant un cadre clair aux priorités et en organisant l’activité quotidienne.

- Anticiper la charge et piloter la capacité de production afin de limiter les bottlenecks et de mieux absorber les variations de volume.

- Construire les outils de pilotage nécessaires pour avoir une vision fine du flux : volumes de patients, capacité de traitement, taux d’erreur, points de blocage et charge de l’équipe.

- Construire et orchestrer une roadmap d’amélioration continue permettant progressivement d’augmenter la capacité de traitement.

- Porter cette roadmap auprès des équipes Produit, IA et Engineering : rendre les besoins opérationnels visibles, suivre les livrables R&D et créer le rythme nécessaire pour que les améliorations soient effectivement délivrées.

- Garantir la qualité des cohortes et contribuer à la préparation des exports de données nécessaires aux projets de recherche.

Ce que nous attendrons de toi

Dans les premiers mois, nous attendrons de toi que tu développes une compréhension très fine du flux Clinical Ops : où se trouvent les blocages, comment évolue la charge et quels leviers permettent réellement d'améliorer la production.

Ton succès se mesurera notamment à ta capacité à mettre en place un pilotage fiable de l’activité, à réduire les erreurs et les bottlenecks et à créer, avec les équipes Produit et R&D, un rythme d’amélioration continue suffisamment soutenu pour accompagner notre changement d’échelle.

À horizon 9 mois, l’objectif est clair : passer d’environ 100–200 à 300–600 cas patients structurés par semaine, sans multiplier les ressources par trois. 

Ce que nous recherchons

Must-have

Nous chercherons en priorité trois éléments dans ton parcours :

- Une expérience réussie en startup ou scale-up , dans un environnement où les process, outils et responsabilités restaient à construire.

- Une expérience concrète de la Real-World Data / Real-World Evidence , idéalement autour de la constitution ou de l'exploitation de cohortes patients.

- Un background santé ou scientifique te permettant de comprendre les enjeux liés aux données médicales et à la recherche clinique.

Nous attendons également :

- Une expérience confirmée de management d’équipe opérationnelle .

- Une expérience de structuration et de pilotage d’une activité complexe à partir de données et de KPI.

- Une capacité à passer d’un problème opérationnel très concret à un plan d’amélioration structuré.

- Une expérience de collaboration étroite avec des équipes Produit, Data/IA ou Engineering .

title: Software Engineer
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role 

As Kernel Software Engineer, you own the low-level software platform that sits between our hardware and the flight application on our ground control stations. You work across the Linux kernel, board support and a custom Android build, so that every control, display and data link works reliably in the field. You are the bridge between our hardware and application teams, taking a new product line from board bring-up to mass production.

Responsibilities 

- Bring up, configure and maintain the Linux kernel on our hardware, including device tree, drivers and security patches.

- Customize and maintain our Android build, covering system services, permissions, boot sequence and OTA updates.

- Integrate controls, display, touch, battery and radio modules, and expose them cleanly to the application layer.

- Ensure robust, low-latency SBUS and MAVLink data flows between the controller, the radio and the drone.

- Debug hardware and software issues alongside electronics and mechanical engineers, using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and UART/JTAG.

- Define flashing, provisioning, factory test and release procedures with the production team.

- Work with QGroundControl engineers and QA to validate system behavior on real hardware.

- Join field tests and flight sessions to validate your work in real conditions.

Candidate Requirements 

- Master’s degree in Embedded Systems, Software Engineering, Electronics or a related field.

- 3+ years of experience in embedded software development.

- Strong command of the Linux kernel (configuration, device tree, drivers, debugging) and of C; C++ is a plus.

- Hands-on background customizing AOSP, from HALs and system services to the build system.

- Comfortable at the hardware boundary: UART, SPI, I2C, GPIO, USB, display and touch controllers.

- Exposure to drones or robotics, including MAVLink or PX4/ArduPilot, is a plus.

- Hands-on, autonomous and pragmatic, with curiosity about hardware and the ability to learn quickly.

- Professional English for technical documentation and international collaboration.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Nous recherchons des commerciaux terrain expérimentés, à l’aise pour se rendre dans une entreprise, engager la conversation avec le propriétaire et convaincre de nouveaux commerçants.

Vous devrez justifier d’une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.

Vos missions

- Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.

- Cibler les entreprises locales générant d’importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.

- Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d’optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.

- Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.

Ce que nous recherchons

Indispensable

- Au moins un an d’expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l’énergie, les technologies d’entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l’approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.

- Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects.

- Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.

Atouts

- Un réseau existant de chefs d’entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp.

Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain.

Rémunération

Il s’agit d’une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l’activité des commerçants apportés.

Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner :

- Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions.

- Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème.

- Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème.

- Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans.

Les nouveaux partenaires bénéficient des conditions Partner pendant la période de lancement. Leur maintien est ensuite soumis aux critères d’activité du programme ; un barème Agent de 40 %, sans commissions résiduelles, peut s’appliquer.

Les conditions d’éligibilité, les bases de calcul et les modalités de versement sont précisées dans le contrat et présentées avant tout engagement. Les commissions s’entendent avant déduction de vos frais professionnels, cotisations sociales et impôts applicables.

Nous vous aiderons à vous familiariser avec les produits et leur commercialisation grâce à un parcours initial et à un accompagnement continu couvrant la prospection, les entretiens de vente, les démonstrations, la gestion des objections et l’accompagnement des clients.

Les modalités du parcours initial et les prérequis à la commercialisation vous seront communiqués avant le démarrage.

Votre interlocuteur SumUp vous apportera également son soutien en matière de développement territorial, d’analyse de vos opportunités et de conseils commerciaux, dans le respect de votre autonomie d’organisation.

description:
About us 

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

Role Summary 

We're looking for an SMB Go-To-Market Lead to own how Photoroom wins established eCommerce merchants doing €500K to tens of millions in GMV (gross merchandise value, i.e., annual online sales).

You come from the eCommerce world. You know where these merchants spend their time, which platforms they run on (Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, TikTok Shop, and the agencies and apps around them), and which channels actually move them. You've already acquired merchants at this scale, and you've done it with campaigns people talked about.

This is a lead role. You'll ship campaigns yourself every month, and you'll lead a team of 2 GTM managers focused on dedicated personas. This is a marketing lead role for someone who still loves making the work, not a manager who has stopped shipping. 

Compensation: €80,000 – €110,000 + BSPCE

Location: Paris, in-office 3 days per week

About the Role 

- Own SMB merchant acquisition and revenue - Set the GTM strategy for established eCommerce brands and own the numbers behind it: new merchant acquisition and conversion to paid users. Report on them monthly, and decide where the next euro goes across your channels.

- Build the B2B channels we don't have yet - Set up and scale outbound, partnerships (eCom platforms, app ecosystems, agencies, marketplaces), in-person events, and LinkedIn. Find which ones work for merchants at €500K+ GMV, prove them, then turn them into repeatable playbooks.

- Create campaigns people talk about - Concept, write, and ship launch and brand campaigns that spread across eCommerce communities and social feeds. You have the creative idea and know how to distribute it.

title: Communications Lead
description:
Who we are 

Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves.

We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow.

Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education.

Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

About this role 

Yubo doesn't have a PR team yet, and that's exactly why this role exists: to build one from scratch and help Yubo become culturally relevant, resilient to reputational bumps, and a real driver of growth.

It's a rare chance to shape a PR function from day one inside a fast-moving global tech company. You'll design how it works, lead our agency partner, and craft the stories, moments and relationships that make people pay attention to Yubo. The role covers everyday consumer stories, corporate communications, and handling sensitive issues or crises when they arise. To start, you'll focus on the US, UK and France, with room to grow from there.

You'll report to the Director of Brand & Communications and work closely with teams across the business, especially Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. You'll own the relationship with our PR agency, making sure they feel like a true extension of the team, and you'll help set up the habits and processes that make PR part of how Yubo works day to day.

This is a freelance role on a 6-month contract, with a target start in Q4 2026.

Your responsibilites 

Set up how PR works at Yubo 

- Build PR operations and onboard Yubo's PR agency, setting clear ways to spot stories, check facts, and turn insight into coverage.

- Dig into Yubo's data to find trends and stories worth telling.

- Build a simple way to report on PR performance, linking coverage and sentiment to awareness and growth.

- Review and embed Yubo's Crisis Comms Playbook.

Plan and run the PR agenda 

- Build Yubo's 2027 PR calendar and strategy, balancing campaigns, cultural moments, and day-to-day press activity.

- Lead proactive and reactive media relations so Yubo speaks with a clear, consistent voice.

- Spot and activate cultural moments through PR, research, events, creator partnerships and other earned activity.

- Team up with Product and Data to build proof points and stories that show what Yubo means to people.

Look after Yubo's reputation 

- Advise senior leaders on reputational opportunities and risks.

- Support corporate communications and reactive issues management when needed.

- Work with Trust & Safety and Legal so Yubo talks about sensitive topics responsibly.

- Help rally the right people internally when a crisis hits.

Who you are 

You're a proactive PR lead with sharp cultural instincts and a track record of creating stories that genuinely earn attention, not just promote launches.

You'll bring:

- Solid PR experience, with real results to show from leading a function or campaign.

- A good read on Gen-Z culture and how 18 to 24 year-olds socialise and engage online.

- Experience turning insight and data into media stories, including digging into data yourself to find the angle.

- A track record of using different levers to earn attention: influencers, experts, events, activations, research, stunts.

- Experience managing and getting the best out of an external PR agency.

- Good judgement under pressure, with experience in issues or crisis communications.

- Strong writing and speaking skills, comfortable with both consumer storytelling and sensitive corporate messaging.

- The ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders.

- A self-starter mindset, with examples of building something from the ground up.

Nice to have, but don't let that stop you:

- Experience in high-growth tech, consumer apps, youth culture, media, entertainment or lifestyle.

- Experience in the US market, including relationships with US media and journalists.

Within a month, you will 

- Get familiar with Yubo's product, mission and community, and where our communications and reputation stand today.

- Meet key people across Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal.

- Start onboarding our PR agency and reviewing the Crisis Comms Playbook.

Within 3 months, you will 

- Have set up solid working habits with the PR agency and cross-functional teams.

- Be well into building the 2027 PR strategy, calendar and measurement framework.

- Have embedded the Crisis Comms Playbook and be actively building relationships with consumer, culture, lifestyle, tech and business media.

Within 6 months, you will 

- Have delivered Yubo's finished 2027 PR strategy and calendar.

- Have landed our first standout data- and culture-led stories in top-tier media, backed by a working way to measure PR performance.

- Have wrapped up the agency onboarding and defined the role of creators, experts, events and activations in Yubo's communications, leaving a solid foundation for what's next.

The recruitment process 

- A first introductory call with Nicolas, Talent Acquisition

- A case study with Alex, our Brand Director.

Our approach to privacy & safety 

As part of your role, you may handle tools and features involving personal data. We expect all employees to demonstrate strong awareness of privacy and safety issues, and to actively support our Privacy & Safety by Design efforts.

Join Yubo and help shape the future of Social Discovery while enjoying a culture that values flexibility, well-being, and impact.

Here’s how we live our mission every day:

Y ou own the impact: Step up, adapt, and make it matter

U nconventionally Smart: Hack with intent, borrow smart, build better

B e Bold & Resilient: Raise your head, break barriers, keep moving forward

O ne team, one mission: No egos, no passengers, just shared wins

Trust & Flexibility: Our hybrid model calls for only two office days a month; the rest is up to the rhythm that works best for you.

Enjoy Top-notch Benefits

Culture is central at Yubo, hence the numerous benefits:

Cool Workplace : enjoy our amazing Parisian office and our many hybrid work options

Team Activities : participate in get-togethers, events, and team-building activities

Family-Friendly : we support parents with childcare options and family-friendly policies

Wellness Programs : benefit from comprehensive health insurance, wellness programs, sports classes, and mental well-being initiatives

title: Infrastructure Engineer (ML Systems) - Paris
description:
You’ll own the GPU compute that powers our model training, evaluation and serving systems.

This role sits in our Infrastructure team, which works at the lowest layers of our stack, from Kubernetes down to the GPU hardware. You’ll run the clusters, GPUs and schedulers that our research, product and platform teams depend on, and manage the capacity we buy from our cloud providers.

What success looks like

Success is measured by how well we use our GPUs: keeping production reliable and improving the performance of our training and serving stack.

What you’ll be doing

- Running Kubernetes clusters for GPU training and inference

- Improving how GPU work is scheduled and placed

- Detecting, draining and repairing unhealthy GPU nodes

- Managing capacity with our cloud providers

- Debugging failures in GPUs, Linux, storage and networking

The first year

By month 3, you’ll be handling a share of cluster incidents on your own and will have shipped one change to scheduling or node health, such as automatically detecting and draining unhealthy GPU nodes. By month 6, you’ll own one part of the compute layer outright: scheduling and placement, node health and repair, or capacity and new regions. By month 12, you’ll be responsible for a globally distributed GPU system that shifts capacity between training and inference as needs change.

Who you’ll work with

Your hiring manager is our VP of Engineering. Day to day, you’ll work with the Platform Infrastructure team, the research and product teams who use our compute, and our cloud providers and other vendors.

What we think it takes

You’re likely a good fit if you: 

- Have built and run GPU workloads on Kubernetes

- Could design a GPU cluster for training and online RL from scratch

- Debug confidently at the OS layer and below (Linux, GPU drivers, networking and storage)

- Write strong Python

It’s a plus if you’ve worked as an SRE or infrastructure engineer, or have used: 

- Slurm

- Kubernetes scheduling and autoscaling tools such as Kueue or Karpenter

- Multi-cloud orchestration tools such as SkyPilot

- AWS services such as EKS or SageMaker HyperPod

- High-performance interconnects and collective communication libraries such as EFA, InfiniBand, NCCL or Open MPI

- Terraform

You don’t need ML research experience. If you match most of this but not every point, please apply.

How we hire

Four stages, about three hours in total: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute coding interview, a 60-minute system design interview and a closing 30-minute conversation with our VP of Engineering. The coding and system design interviews are modelled on real-world problems you’d face in this role.

Practicalities

The role is hybrid, with three days a week in our Paris or London office and occasional travel between the two. We offer a competitive package.

title: Product Designer - Paris
description:
As a Product Designer, you'll work on the H Platform, where our users create and run agentic AI workflows powered by our models. Nobody has written the playbook for designing these experiences yet. Our next stage is making the platform truly useful for its users and levelling it up, in design as much as in technology, and you'll build the product experiences that deliver real value in organisations.

At H Company, we believe AI should take action in the real world, and our mission is to make agentic AI genuinely useful for large organisations. We're pioneers in computer use: our own vision-language models power agents that see, click and type their way through the software businesses already run, with no integrations or rebuilds, and we own the whole stack, from research and models to the products built on top of them.

What you'll be doing

- Talking to our users constantly to understand their needs and figure out what will make the platform truly useful for them.

- Turning those insights into research and explorations, looking at problems from different angles before settling on a direction.

- Picking the right tool for each task: a Figma design, a prototype, or a small PR when a quick change is the fastest way to ship.

- Testing what you build with users, measuring its impact (A/B testing, user interviews, users daily use data...) and iterating quickly based on what you learn.

- Shaping the roadmap together with the whole team, engineers and PMs alike.

Who you'll work with

The role sits in our Product team, which is responsible for product direction, strategy and design. You'll join the product designer who owns design and UX today, and work closely with product, engineering and forward deployed engineers.

What we think it takes

Above all, we want someone who cares deeply about users, has great product taste and can explain it, moves fast while keeping quality high, leaves their ego at the door and welcomes feedback.

Likely a good fit if you 

- Have 5+ years of experience as a Product Designer at tech companies.

- Have excellent UX, UI and interaction design skills, and can make complex, technical flows, like building and running AI agent workflows, feel simple and intuitive.

- Have a portfolio that shows your latest work.

- Have hands-on experience running user tests and A/B tests.

- Know when a proven solution is good enough and when a problem deserves something new.

- Have designed complex data or ML/AI-driven products: you know how to make complex systems understandable and how to design for AI behaviour that isn't always predictable, building trust and keeping users in control.

- Are comfortable in technical discussions: you can dig into constraints and trade-offs with engineers and ramp up quickly on technical topics to discuss them with our researchers and more technical engineers.

- Are fluent in Figma.

- Can work within a design system and contribute to it.

Stronger still if you 

- Have designed platforms: complex B2B web or desktop software used by professionals, whether that's tools to build and run workflows, big data and analytics software, operational dashboards or other data-dense interfaces.

- Are curious about code and AI in your design workflow. Every design team is still figuring out how AI changes the way we work, and we're no different, so we'd love someone who has started experimenting, whether by prototyping in code, building small tools or bringing AI into their process, and who wants to keep exploring with us.

If you match most of this but not every point, apply anyway. We care far more about how you think, your curiosity and your care for users than a perfect match.

How we hire

Four stages: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute portfolio review, a 60-minute design interview in person at our Paris office, and a closing 30-minute conversation.

The portfolio review and design interview are built around your own work and how you design. Please apply with your CV and a link to your portfolio showing your latest work.

title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions.

You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators.

This is a hands-on scientific leadership role . You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme.

You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions.

The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work.

What You'll Do

Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve.

Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality.

Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses.

Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims.

Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes.

Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations.

Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks.

Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications.

Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations.

Minimum Qualifications

- PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology.

- Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings.

- Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors , including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions.

- A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health , with clear intellectual and analytical contributions.

- Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures.

- Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations.

- Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English , including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning.

- Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow.

- Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints.

- Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling.

- Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners.

- Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements.

- Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network.

Who You Are

- A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time.

- A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems.

- Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly.

- Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods.

- An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress.

Why Join Orakl

- Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions.

- Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together.

- Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data.

- Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions.

- Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme.

- Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support.

- Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme.

Interview Process

- HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

- Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity.

- Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue.

- Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership.

- Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions.

title: Ingénieure ou ingénieur de recherche – Captage du CO₂
description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain .

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École. 

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques. 

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret. 

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité. 

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins. 

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité. 

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’ industrie du futur. 

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ? 

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous 

En tant qu’ Ingénieur(e), vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de neutralité carbone de la France.

Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600).

Ce recrutement est au cœur de la stratégie d’innovation de Mines Saint-Etienne pour permettre à un brevet IMT de se concrétiser en une technologie permettant de capter le CO2 des fumées industrielles, et de contribuer ainsi à l’atteinte de l’objectif Français de Neutralité carbone

· Vous assurez le développement d’un pilote de captage du CO2,

· Vous participez au transfert de technologie entre une méthodologie brevetée et la spin-off Carbon Cage,

· Vous contribuez à un enjeu majeur de notre société,

· Vous rendez compte l’équipe GasHyDyn qui soutient les développements méthodologiques, et vous interagissez au quotidien avec sa spin-off Carbon Cage.

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir.

🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous êtes titulaire d’un :

· Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent,

Et idéalement :

· Titulaire d’une thèse

· Junior accepté : [oui]

• Une expérience significative sur le domaine des clathrates hydrates

• Une maîtrise de l’anglais (niveau C1)

Vos atouts supplémentaires :

• Capacité à travailler dans un contexte international et multiculturel

• Capacité à travailler avec une startup

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde . 

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver : 

· Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain 

· Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an 

· Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail. 

Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science , l’ ingénierie , et des projets qui font sens .

Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures. 

Informations complémentaires

Staff Product Manager – E-Commerce Web Upper Funnel [Permanent - CDI] (f/m/d) 

Location: Paris or Lille, France

Team: Decathlon E-Commerce Web – Scope Upper Funnel

About the Team 

At the heart of Decathlon’s global digital ecosystem, our E-Commerce Web team builds the online destination for millions of sports lovers worldwide. The Upper Funnel scope is the front door of our digital experience: from landing on the homepage and navigating categories, to discovering products via search, AI-driven recommendations, conversational shopping, retail media placements, and inspiring content. Our mission is to seamlessly guide users from inspiration to intent.

Joining this high-traffic Web Product organization means operating at massive scale where speed, discovery excellence, SEO, targeted monetization, and next-gen personalized user journeys drive our everyday business impact.

YOUR FUTURE CONTRIBUTION 

As a Staff Product Manager – Upper Funnel , you will provide the strategic direction, functional architecture, and product leadership needed to scale and modernize the discovery and exploration experience across Decathlon's web platform. Operating with high autonomy, you will address complex challenges across search performance, catalog structuring, retail media integration, and emerging AI paradigm shifts like conversational interface models and agentic workflows.

Your mission centers on 4 strategic pillars:

1. Strategic Alignment, Stakeholder Management & Upper Funnel Vision 

- Own the Holistic Discovery & Engagement Strategy : Define and drive the strategic vision for upper funnel web touchpoints (Homepage, Category/Listing Pages, Search Engine, Navigation Taxonomy, Retail Media Ad Placements, Conversational Assistants, and Inspiration Hubs).

- Executive & Cross-Functional Alignment : Partner with global business directors, commercial/merchandising leads, SEO specialists, retail media monetization teams, and AI platform engineering leads to align executive leadership around major web platform shifts and discovery roadmaps.

- Macro Metrics & Funnel Performance : Track, measure, and optimize key upper funnel metrics across the customer journey: Organic/Direct Traffic, Search CTR, Category Depth, Conversational Engagement & Intent Resolution Rate, Ad Yield/eCPM, Bounce Rate, Product Detail Page (PDP) Click-through Rate, and Top-of-Funnel Conversion.

2. Functional Architecture & Web Ecosystem Orchestration 

- Lead Functional Architect : Define boundary maps and functional scope across web squads (Search & Conversational Discovery, Taxonomy & Merchandising, Personalization/Recommendations, Retail Media & Sponsored Listings) to eliminate overlap and friction.

- Tight Triad Collaboration : Work in close sync with Staff/Principal Web Engineers and Staff UX/UI Designers to align frontend performance (Core Web Vitals), modular web design systems, micro-frontend architecture, conversational UI patterns, and backend search/ad-serving APIs.

- Seamless Omnichannel & Funnel Handoff : Ensure fluid transitions from external acquisition channels into the web upper funnel, balancing organic product discovery and agentic assistance with sponsored/retail media inventory while designing seamless handoffs toward the lower funnel (PDP, Cart & Checkout).

3. Strategic Sparring & Product De-Risking 

- Trusted Strategic Advisor : Serve as a sparring partner for Group Product Managers (GPMs) and Product Managers (PMs) within the Web & E-Commerce domain, helping them navigate complex search algorithms, LLM agent architectures, ad server integrations, taxonomy dependencies, and high-volume web constraints.

- De-Risking High-Stakes Initiatives : Formulate and execute validation strategies for high-risk discovery and monetization concepts (e.g., visual/voice search, conversational product advisors, agentic auto-replenishment/bundles, sponsored product placements).

- Continuous Experimentation at Scale : Design and lead high-volume A/B and multivariate testing strategies, balancing conversational interaction models and ad impression density against organic conversion performance using CRO frameworks and Opportunity Solution Trees (OST).

4. Elevating Product Craft & Modern Web Capabilities 

- AI-First, Agentic & Monetization Leadership : Champion the organizational adoption of cloud-native AI platforms (e.g., Google Vertex AI), conversational frameworks, agentic e-commerce patterns, and modern retail media capabilities to amplify both user experience and platform revenue.

- Web Craft & Best Practices : Upskill the PM community in modern web product practices, continuous discovery frameworks, technical web performance optimization, and data-informed decision-making.

- Community Multiplier : Elevate the overall bar of the Product Management organization as a thought leader without acting as a direct line manager.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE 

- E-Commerce Web Scale (7+ years) : Proven track record in Product Management with hands-on experience scaling high-traffic e-commerce web platforms (Upper Funnel, Search, Merchandising, or Navigation).

- Upper Funnel & SEO Expertise : Deep understanding of top-of-funnel mechanics, technical SEO, site search algorithms, taxonomy design, and conversion rate optimization (CRO).

- Data & Discovery Mastery : Strong expertise in web analytics (GA4/Amplitude/Contentsquare), high-traffic A/B testing frameworks, quantitative/qualitative user research, and Opportunity Solution Trees (OST).

- Functional Architecture & Scoping : Ability to decompose complex e-commerce catalog, ad-tech, and AI/search problems into modular MVP/V0/V1 execution strategies.

- Executive Storytelling & Alignment : Exceptional ability to translate complex search/agentic architectures, retail media revenue drivers, UX metrics, and conversion data into compelling narratives for executive stakeholders.

- Key Pluses & Emerging Tech Strengths :

- Google Vertex AI : Practical experience using Google Vertex AI (for Search, Recommendations, or custom ML/LLM model deployment) is a major plus.

- Conversational & Agentic E-Commerce : Solid understanding or experience with conversational AI interfaces (chat/voice product advisors) and agentic commerce concepts (autonomous intent-matching, task-oriented AI agents) is a strong plus.

- Retail Media & Monetization : Experience with Retail Media concepts and ad management (sponsored products, ad-server integrations, balancing yield vs. UX) is a major plus.

- Soft Skills & Leadership : Strong strategic influence, ability to thrive in ambiguity, passion for cross-functional collaboration in Triad, and an empathetic approach to mentoring junior PMs.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU 

- Hybrid Work Model (Paris or Lille base) 2 days of remote work per week

- Tailored Equipment (Mac or Windows, according to mission and sustainability commitments);

- Global Exposure : Local project team within a global retail and digital network with international career opportunities;

- Continuous Growth : Internal/external trainings, skill development programs, and conference attendance;

- Comprehensive Compensation : Competitive salary package including employee stock ownership, profit-sharing, and monthly/quarterly performance bonuses.

DECATHLON DIGITAL CONTEXT 

What if technology allowed us to push the boundaries and take sports experiences to new levels? That's exactly our goal at Decathlon Digital! We are a team of 5,000+ experts in software engineering, product management, data, cloud, and cybersecurity, distributed across Paris, Lille, and Amsterdam. Together, we are creating the largest digital sports platform, leveraging tech innovation from design to value chain optimization, connected experiences and product second life.

Changing the game for good . We are in this for the love of sports. And like everything we love, we want it to last. That’s why we are embarking on a journey to create a more sustainable tech model, reducing our direct environmental impact while maintaining a safe, diverse, and inclusive space for all our people to learn and thrive together. Team up with us to design the digital future of sports.

title: Embedded System Lead Engineer
description:
Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR 

Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders 

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats.

France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa , the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.

The role

As Embedded System Lead Engineer , you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it.

What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget.

You will lead their technical development , from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come.

These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge , on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role.

The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it.

What you'll own

- Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications.

- The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt.

- Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS).

- The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment.

- Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore.

- Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench.

- Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units.

The hard problems you'll be solving

These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point:

- Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling.

- Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell.

- Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible.

- Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it.

- Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean.

Who we're looking for

You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically:

- 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world.

- Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems . This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space.

- Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack : electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal.

- Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control.

- Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do.

- A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters.

- Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it.

Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale.

Why join now

- Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that.

- A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space.

- Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years.

- AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about.

- A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it.

title: Legal AI Engineer (Zurich)
description:
Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.

Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.

Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.

Why us? - Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
- No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
- We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
- Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
- Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
- Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.

Process - Expectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.
- Depth. A conversation with our General Counsel & Head of Legal AI on Legal Engineering at Legartis and where the legal market is going.
- Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves.
- Meet the team in our Zurich office.
- A mutual decision, before we welcome you to the team.

About the role 

ElevenLabs is looking for a Value Strategist to help our customers identify, quantify, and realize the business value of ElevenLabs across our portfolio, with a primary focus on ElevenAgents.

You will work directly with customers and prospects to understand their businesses, build the case for investment, and establish how that value will be measured over time.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

In this role you will 

- Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on 
  
In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. About BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. 

BridgeBio is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing, and delivering transformative medicines for patients living with genetic diseases and genetically defined cancers. Since our founding in 2015, we have built a diverse portfolio of more than 20 drug development programs, ranging from early discovery to late-stage clinical trials, across multiple therapeutic areas including precision oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, and renal disease. We have already achieved regulatory approval for three therapies and continue to advance promising science from academia into meaningful treatments for patients worldwide. 

Who We Are 

BridgeBio is a global biotechnology company with our Global Headquarters located in San Francisco, USA, and our International HQ located in Zug, Switzerland. Since establishing our European presence in 2021, we’ve been building empowered, high-performing teams across countries — with experienced colleagues who move quickly, take ownership, and are fueling the company’s international growth. 

At BridgeBio, you’ll find an energetic and collaborative culture where pragmatism meets bold decision-making. We embrace uncertainty with confidence, guided by our commitment to making a meaningful impact for patients.
